dependsOnUnavailable: this instance has not declared `publishable`, so §3.4's record is withheld rather than asserted — undecided, never false (§3.1, §6 Q1)

@graph.name: theme-art-intake
@graph.title: Theme art intake
@graph.description: Accept or refuse a set of three theme/avatar layouts arriving through document ingestion, with a named reason for every refusal.

@graph.name: site-presentation-assets
@graph.title: Site presentation assets — the node is the source, the stylesheet is a rendering
@graph.description: A visual fact — a colour, a glyph, a theme — lives in a graph node, and the stylesheet the site serves is a rendering of it. Read before adding a colour, an icon or a theme, before hand-editing any generated stylesheet, and before referencing a generated asset from a page.

@graph.name: theme-declaration
@graph.title: Declaring a theme
@graph.description: What a theme IS as data — the palette, the three required layouts, and the per-image regions (`textRegion`, `avatarRegion`). The PRODUCER stage: this is where a number is written down, and the rule is that geometry over art is declared rather than derived, because no amount of arithmetic on an aspect ratio can see where a picture is quiet.

@graph.name: theming
@graph.title: Theming, split on the stage it fails at
@graph.description: The map of this subgraph: theming is split on PIPELINE STAGE first — intake, declaration, generation, contrast — with producer/consumer as the direction each stage faces, and per-artefact specialisation last. Read this to find which stage owns the fact you need; read the stage for the fact.

@graph.name: theme-contrast
@graph.title: Contrast: measured over the darkest thing that could be there
@graph.description: Why every scrim is measured over PURE BLACK rather than over the art actually in use, what the AAA floor is, and why the high-contrast pair declares no backdrop at all. The CONSUMER stage that says what the ink must survive.

@graph.name: create-sticky-note
@graph.title: Create a sticky note
@graph.description: Draft a sticky note from the conversation, choose its theme and its place, preview it, and only then attach it to a node.

@graph.name: theme-artefacts
@graph.title: Per-artefact specialisation
@graph.description: The per-surface SPECIALISATION layer — sticky, landing board, docs background, navbar avatar. Only what DIFFERS lives here; the general rule lives in its stage. Read this last, after the stage that owns your question.

@graph.name: theme-generation
@graph.title: Generating a theme's CSS
@graph.description: Turning a declared theme into CSS — `bun run themes:css` — and the single consumer-side failure this stage exists to stop: a theme with no CSS rule falls back to an opaque surface and paints over its own art. Four rounds of "still not image" had that one cause.

@graph.name: kg-navigation
@graph.title: Reading the knowledge graph — how to find the skill you need
@graph.description: How a cold agent finds and loads the skill that governs its task. The two Tools that serve the knowledge graph — the MCP pair and the filesystem fallback — what counts as a skill, and the three ways the search goes wrong.

@graph.name: dak-postprocessing
@graph.title: dak-postprocessing
@graph.description: What the DAK post-processing phase accomplishes after the IG Publisher runs — the JSON/JSON-LD surface, the DAK API hub, and the metadata-to-Liquid bridge that is the seam the just-the-docs transition cuts at. Read before changing a post-processing step, and before assuming the Publisher produced something it did not.

@graph.name: smart-stack-layering
@graph.title: smart-stack-layering
@graph.description: Which of the five layers a WHO SMART asset, rule, script or page belongs to, and the one question that settles it. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, smart-base, smart-l1, smart-dak or smart-ig, before creating a per-IG harness, and before moving a pre/post-processing step.

@graph.name: dak-preprocessing
@graph.title: dak-preprocessing
@graph.description: What the DAK pre-processing phase actually accomplishes, step by step, before the IG Publisher runs — and which of its steps exist only to satisfy the Publisher's own page index. Read before changing a pre-processing step, before assuming one is needed, and before moving one to another layer.

@graph.name: toolchain-ownership
@graph.title: toolchain-ownership
@graph.description: Taking ownership of the WHO smart-base scripts in a litlfred fork, rewriting them to the Skill I/O contract, and the one gate that governs when a script may actually move. Read before touching, copying or rewriting any upstream smart-base script.

@graph.name: edge-kinds-and-blast-radius
@graph.title: consulted: reference material nobody performs — a PRINCIPLE about graph semantics. Zero imperative markers and every heading is a claim — "Not every edge is a dependency", "Provenance is three-valued", "Taint propagates down the dependency graph". It is read before deciding how to traverse a graph; nobody performs it as a task.
@graph.description: A graph has more than one kind of edge, and conflating them corrupts both the ordering and the impact answer. Interface edges versus implementation edges, the union rule for blast radius, and the split/merge signals — generalized out of the formal-math skills that first stated them.

@graph.name: graph-detanglement
@graph.title: Graph detanglement — the practice, not the migration
@graph.description: Drive a tangled graph toward a clean partition, so a sub-graph can be split off when it grows too large or when a business reason separates it. The staged practice — declare in place, detangle, isolate, extract — with the seventeen moves that were measured rather than argued, and the failures each one cost.

@graph.name: graph-rendering
@graph.title: Graph rendering: one set of rules for every drawn graph
@graph.description: Draw any graph in a harness (schemas, processes, a paper's block graph, a Lean proof's dependencies, a detangle partition) so the picture is derived, checkable and readable. Ten rules learned on the UML overview, which engine to lay a graph out with and why, and how each graph kind here applies them.

@graph.name: domain-fencing
@graph.title: Domain fencing — keeping one folio's rules out of everybody's platform
@graph.description: How a domain-specific rule is kept out of the platform without being lost — the opt-in axis mechanism, the one criterion that should use it and does not, and the test for whether a rule generalizes at all.

@graph.name: crdm-data-model
@graph.title: CRDM — the data-modelling phase
@graph.description: The CRDM data-modelling phase — when in the requirements process a model is built, what it is built from, who confirms it, and what it hands to the phases either side. The technique it invokes is `data-modelling`; this skill carries only the sequencing and the sign-off.

@graph.name: issue-working
@graph.title: Working an issue — announce, then re-check
@graph.description: Working a tracked issue — announce the branch when you create it rather than when you finish, and re-check the issue for new AND edited comments while you work. Both rules are about the gap between your view of an issue and everyone else's.

@graph.name: exposition-swarm-drain
@graph.title: /exposition-swarm-drain — Milnor-exposition audit→resolve drain
@graph.description: Drain the paper's narrative blocks through an exposition-quality swarm: a small fleet of grouped-batch agents each audit their batch against the Milnor exposition gate (expo-milnor-clarity, H1–H8) plus the deterministic narrative defect checks (proof-sketch-vs-kind, proof-no-lean-mention-in-prose, proof-cross-block-duplication), then RESOLVE the flagged blocks with conservative, math-preserving edits. Each swarm agent owns its own branch (commits, pushes, opens a PR); the foreground session runs auto prepare-merge on each swarm branch and repeats batch-by-batch until the paper is completely drained. Sister to `/integration-backlog` (that drains watcher findings; this drains exposition quality).

@graph.name: todo-review
@graph.title: Todo Review Skill
@graph.description: Monitor and triage open feedback across all content blocks. At session start, ask the author if they'd like to work on feedback. Provide overview, let them pick a chapter/section, then review and iterate until done.

@graph.name: render-order
@graph.title: Render order — flattening a dependency hierarchy, and the two stages

@graph.name: translation-manager
@graph.title: Translation manager
@graph.description: Translation lifecycle management for folio content. Covers gettext PO/POT extraction and injection, TranslationNode manifests as KG nodes, official vs unofficial translations, staleness tracking, sign-off workflow, automatic badge rendering, and the poSources fallback resolution chain.

@graph.name: tabular-metadata
@graph.title: Tabular metadata — CSVW, annotated, and honest about what it could not read
@graph.description: Extract tabular metadata from a CSV or spreadsheet as CSVW — tables, rows, headers, columns, datatypes and location on sheet — recording every field as determined or explicitly undetermined. Read before touching a tabular ingest arm, adding a format, or deciding what a sheet is in the graph.

@graph.name: covered-is-not-reachable
@graph.title: Covered is not reachable — and `check:tools` cannot tell you which
@graph.description: A skill can be satisfied by the neighbours of its mechanism while the mechanism is reachable from no Tool node. Read before concluding from check:tools that a command is reachable, and before adding a Tool node or a `maintains` claim.

@graph.name: uml-overview
@graph.title: UML overview: generated from declarations and schemas, never drawn
@graph.description: Read, regenerate or extend the UML class diagrams of a harness: one per harness and one per named sub-graph it declares, plus the harness object model. Every box is generated from a declaration and a schema, never drawn by hand, so a wrong diagram is fixed at the declaration or the schema, and a dashed "could not determine" box is a finding about the registry.

@graph.name: milnor-exposition-standard
@graph.title: The Milnor exposition standard
@graph.description: The eight hallmarks of mathematical exposition, scored 0-2 with sixteen the only passing total, derived from John Milnor's "Link Groups" (1954). The author-facing half of the `expo-milnor-clarity` strict gate; three of its findings contradict the general house voice and say so.

@graph.name: pickup
@graph.title: Pickup Skill
@graph.description: Pick up / continue work on one or more existing open PRs efficiently. Resolves each PR's REAL branch + title + checklist + reviews + CI in one batched pass, classifies CI as billing-vs-real, then dispatches one worktree sub-agent per PR with a filled-in brief, and applies the safe class of review-nit fixes (eval→ast.literal_eval, dead-code/unused-var removal, etc.). Use when the user says "pick up PR N", "continue 1543/1576/1571", "work these PRs", "address the review on PR N", or "take over PR N".

@graph.name: swot-analysis
@graph.title: Running a SWOT scan
@graph.description: Running a SWOT situation analysis — the four activities of `swot-analysis.bpmn`, what each step must produce, and the one thing the technique must never be used for. The method itself lives in the `methodology` graph and is not repeated here.

@graph.name: technical-documentation
@graph.title: Technical documentation
@graph.description: Write and review technical documentation of standards, software and knowledge assets as an SDO writes. Carries the RFC 2119 requirement levels as RFC 8174 constrains them, the three questions a first draft is measured against, and the rule that an ingested specification is checked for supersession before it is cited.

@graph.name: confirmation-waiver
@graph.title: A confirmation can be waived — by the person who is owed it
@graph.description: A human may waive a confirmation they are owed — for a session, for a process run, or until a stated time. Covers what a waiver is made of, where it is recorded (the context graph, never the work plan), the gates that can be waived and the rules that cannot, why every waiver carries an expiry, and the one thing an agent may never do: grant itself one.

@graph.name: integration-audit
@graph.title: /integration-audit — invalidate + re-audit the sidecar pipeline
@graph.description: Sidecar-invalidation utility for the integration-watcher pipeline. Adds mechanical QA fields (script-reviewer entries) to per-block `.qa.json` sidecars and marks the existing entries stale so the next `qa-sweep` re-evaluates them. Use when a checker bug is fixed in a QA checker module (downstream "fresh" entries are now incorrect) or when a registry update adds a criterion the block hasn't been audited under.

@graph.name: mcp-assembly
@graph.title: MCP assembly — many Tools, one service, one namespace
@graph.description: Compose several Tool nodes into one MCP service — naming, collisions, grouping and versioning. Read when a service will expose more than one tool, or when two instances' tools land in the same namespace.

@graph.name: content-context-and-state-graphs
@graph.title: Content, context and state graphs
@graph.description: Every declared graph is the subject a process produces, static context it reads, or live state it writes. The one question that settles it, the classification of every kind with its reason, what a consumer may assume of each layer, and why agent memory is context rather than state.

@graph.name: opening-brief
@graph.title: Opening brief — brief the topic before you touch anything
@graph.description: Brief a bean or a topic BEFORE touching anything: what you are doing and why it is worth doing, what you already know and with what provenance, how you plan to do it and what would falsify the approach. Scales with irreversibility, not line count.

@graph.name: production-vs-exploratory-discipline
@graph.title: Production vs exploratory vs numerology — the bright-line guide
@graph.description: Distinguish PRODUCTION (derived-only, no fits) from EXPLORATORY (empirical-fit probes OK as shape-hints) from NUMEROLOGY (post-hoc fits to known constants). The hidden-extra-input / empirical-fit antipattern is a common review-churn source: agents promote empirical fits into production scripts, "closed" status, dashboards, and named constants without a derivation. This skill is the bright-line guide for which output goes where, the derivation-menu check, and the escalation path for off-menu coefficients.

@graph.name: voice-editorial-review
@graph.title: Voice editorial review
@graph.description: Adjudicate a `voice-*` finding — read the flagged passage as a reader of THAT genre would and decide whether the register is wrong, the criterion is out of scope, or the block is a stated exception. The human/agent half of the voice QA axis; the mechanical half runs in `qa-checkers-voice.ts`.

@graph.name: agent-memory
@graph.title: Subagent memory — what a durable entry may claim
@graph.description: Durable memory for a subagent — the three entry labels and what each promises, why entries are authored as graph nodes rather than in the generated file, the injection budget that silently truncates, and archiving as the third state between "reaches everybody" and "deleted".

@graph.name: goal-review
@graph.title: Goal review — cold start, sweep a window, prioritise against stated goals
@graph.description: Cold start, then review a time window of activity — sibling sessions, the work plan, issues, change proposals, branches, CI — and prioritise what it finds against goals stated in the owner's words. Inputs are the window, the goals, the scope and the axes; the output is a synopsis (closed, open, needs doing, with effort), a priority queue per goal with selectable next actions, and the instruction gaps met on the way, each recorded as a work item. Use when asked "what happened", "what is stalled", "what should we do next for X", or at the start of a session that inherits parallel work.

@graph.name: block-density
@graph.title: Block Density — Topic Coherence and Table Extraction Skill
@graph.description: Audits individual content blocks for single-topic coherence, length, and embedded tables.  Blocks that cover multiple topics or exceed ~2/3 of a page should be split; large tables (>5 rows) must be their own `table` block.  Child blocks from a split may belong in different chapters than the parent.

@graph.name: repo-conversion
@graph.title: /repo-conversion — folio-assistant over a repo that already has a life
@graph.description: Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, or asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along.

@graph.name: content-acquisition
@graph.title: Acquisition is the step before ingestion, and it had no home
@graph.description: Getting a resource INTO the graph in the first place — accepting one offered unprompted, or asking for one and then asking for it to be uploaded. The channels are plural and open: `uploads/` is one, the conversation is another. Runs before document ingestion, which begins only once a file has landed.

@graph.name: mcp-projection
@graph.title: consulted: reference material nobody performs — EXPLAINS a mapping — Tool node to MCP service — and instructs nobody. Classified the same way in the y1w9 sample of 15, by reading it, before this pass.
@graph.description: Generate an MCP server from Tool nodes — the mapping from this harness's skill/Tool vocabulary onto the current MCP standard. Read before exposing a CLI tool over MCP, or when asked how an agent stands a service up.

@graph.name: docs-generation
@graph.title: Documentation Generation Skill
@graph.description: Generate and deploy documentation artifacts: schema docs (TypeDoc), formal-layer API docs, dependency graphs, schema manifests, and per-paper HTML/PDF/Markdown outputs.

@graph.name: staging-review
@graph.title: Staging review — before/after comparison
@graph.description: Staging preview and before/after comparison for content review. Takes one optional string — what the reader wants to look at, in their own words — and returns a list of URLs, each looked up in the publish ref, with what is published at it and what to review there. Provides before (MAIN) and after (STAGING) pairs so reviewers can compare rather than guess. Used by the CRDM feature development workflow, content authoring review sessions, and whenever a staging preview deploys or someone asks to see it.

@graph.name: communication-language
@graph.title: The language you communicate in
@graph.description: Determine the language an agent SPEAKS IN — the language of a turn, as against the language of content. Covers the four inputs and their order, why a model's own languages are never the answer, the boundary between speaking to the person and writing durable artefacts, where the determination is recorded so a sibling session does not re-ask, and when to re-ask.

@graph.name: decision-comparison
@graph.title: The comparison goes BEFORE the question, not inside the options
@graph.description: Lay a decision out as a comparison before you ask it — what each option does, its pro, its con, what it changes downstream, and how reversible it is — in the prose that precedes the question, never inside the option labels. Required whenever a choice is handed to a person.

@graph.name: platform-gates
@graph.title: The platform's own gates — run what CI will run
@graph.description: `bun test` passing is not the gates passing. What to run before you push, why the list is derived from the CI workflow rather than written down, and what a `*:check` failure is actually telling you to do.

@graph.name: chapter-complexity-review
@graph.title: Chapter Complexity Review
@graph.description: Analyse a chapter's internal dependency graph to find backward edges (blocks that reference something defined later), compute graph energy, and suggest section/block reorderings that minimise complexity. Uses Graphviz for visualisation and brute-force permutation search for optimal section ordering.

@graph.name: kg-to-portal
@graph.title: KG → package → distribution → portal
@graph.description: Getting a knowledge graph out to a public portal — the six stages between "the graph is in the repository" and "a reader's browser has the bytes", why a CDN is a layer rather than a publication host, and which decisions are the deployment's to make rather than the pipeline's.

@graph.name: docs-auto
@graph.title: docs-auto — the index is generated, the meaning is authored
@graph.description: Derived documentation for a sub-graph — what the handler emits, what it deliberately does not, and the obligation on whoever authors a harness's docs: summarise what the index lists, by reusing it rather than restating it.

@graph.name: where-does-this-go
@graph.title: Where does this go? — the question, then the skill that answers it
@graph.description: The router for filing decisions. This repository answers "where does this go?" nine separate times, each well, and nothing says WHICH question you are asking — so an agent who does not know a rule exists cannot look it up. One discriminating question per row, and the skill that owns the answer.

@graph.name: associate-harness
@graph.title: Associate a harness
@graph.description: Declare a harness this one knows about and does not hold (`associatedHarnesses`): a folio in another repository, published at its own site. Referenced, never loaded, never materialized. Issue #1146.

@graph.name: filing-dublin-core
@graph.title: Filing a source: what Dublin Core carries, and what it does not
@graph.description: Cataloguing a source as it arrives — which facts are `dcterms`, which are this project's own, and why the line is drawn by the vocabulary rather than by convenience. The bibliographic layer only; the derived layer belongs to ingestion.

@graph.name: session-intent
@graph.title: /session-intent — durable session intent + results
@graph.description: Session-start intent declaration + session-end results recording, against the goal-scoped master ledger and queue file. Enforces the durable-handoff discipline so any agent can pick up another's thread.

@graph.name: wireframe-design-review
@graph.title: Wireframe design review
@graph.description: Design a user interface (a page, a visualiser, a navbar) by the WireGen methodology: a written design intent, at least two mid-fidelity HTML candidates, each with a web AND a mobile layout, mechanical checks at both viewports, a blind per-criterion review, adjudication where reviewers disagree, and a recorded choice. Also how an EXISTING visualiser is wireframed as-is, so that every declared visualiser has a wireframe with a QA sidecar. Process: processes/wireframe-design-review.bpmn.

@graph.name: coordinate
@graph.title: /coordinate — multi-agent / multi-PR coordination
@graph.description: Coordinate work across multiple in-flight Claude PRs working toward a shared goal. Post intent + asks on related PRs, identify cherry-pickable work, respond to code-review comments on your own PR, periodically triage sibling PR activity (new comments, CI status, new commits), watch main + newly created branches/PRs, escalate inconsistent findings to the author, and keep a coordination ledger up to date.

@graph.name: where-a-proposal-goes
@graph.title: Where a proposal goes — the issue, not the documentation

@graph.name: glossary-terms
@graph.title: Glossary terms
@graph.description: Add terms to an instance's glossary: local SKOS terms (folio-glossary/v1) with a definition, a code and links to external SKOS concepts, and references to whole external schemes. Rendered on the glossary/ page; gated by check:glossary.

@graph.name: dispatch-agent
@graph.title: /dispatch-agent — parallel dispatch with a live 2-minute status heartbeat
@graph.description: Dispatch one or more background sub-agents against parallel research/build fronts with a STANDARDIZED live progress contract, and monitor them on a 2-minute heartbeat. Every dispatched agent emits consistent DID/DOING/NEXT/BLOCKERS blocks with real log output (not static "still running"); the parent extracts the latest block from each agent every ~120 s and posts one consolidated synthesis table. Use when the user says "dispatch agents", "fan out", "run these in parallel with monitoring", "give me status every 2 minutes", or when you are about to launch ≥ 2 background Agents on independent work.

@graph.name: getting-started
@graph.title: /getting-started — what did they actually ask for?
@graph.description: Triage what a person means when they ask to create a folio, and route them. Five requests share one sentence — a folio in a new repo, folio-assistant overlaid on an existing repo, a second folio in an instance that already has one, a content object they called a folio, or something the filesystem cannot tell apart. Reads the repository facts, runs them through the folio-intent decision table, asks a selectable question for what facts cannot settle, scaffolds, and reports the published URL. Use whenever a user asks to create, start, set up, or initialise a folio, a paper, a DAK, an IG, or "folio-assistant" itself.

@graph.name: qa-report-signing
@graph.title: QA report signing — two routes, chosen by the performer's reach

@graph.name: untainted-verification
@graph.title: Untainted verification — the producer never writes the verdict
@graph.description: The party that produced an artefact does not write the verdict on it. How a checker and an adjudicator are dispatched with controlled context, the three rules that make it a measurement rather than a ritual, and the third state that lets it gate at all.

@graph.name: bib-qa
@graph.title: Bibliography QA Skill
@graph.description: Bibliography quality-assurance agent — validates every reference in content/schema/references.ts against several QA checks: URL availability, URL resolution, metadata completeness, citation coverage, and screenshot/image evidence.  Generates bib-qa.json consumed by the standalone bib-qa.html dashboard.

@graph.name: narrative-asserts-code
@graph.title: Does the prose say what the code does?
@graph.description: Judge whether the prose side of a declared prose ↔ code pair still says what the code does, when the machine could not settle it. Reads the two mechanical signals first — staleness and resolvable claims — and settles what is left in one of three ways, sending a disagreement with a checker to adjudication. General: the Lean case is a specialisation with its own skill.

@graph.name: related-work-coordination
@graph.title: Related work: find it, sort it, ask
@graph.description: Before new work takes shape, find the work it touches. Search beans, issues and open PRs for relevance; categorize and summarize every hit; then ask the user whether and how to coordinate. Judgement decides the categories and the recommendation, and the user decides the coordination. Called by CRDM when a requirement is initiated or updated in chat, and by methodology adoption. Process: processes/related-work.bpmn.

@graph.name: schema-management
@graph.title: Managing a schema — the graph, the viewer, and the three answers that are not "fine"
@graph.description: Manage a schema over its life — add one, change one, read the schema graph and its viewer, and act on what the reader could not determine. The layout rule lives in `directory-conventions`; the entity question lives in `data-modelling`; this is the work in between.

@graph.name: content-profiles
@graph.title: Content types — `document` is the base, a paper extends it
@graph.description: Adapters and profiles are different axes and conflating them is costly. What a document folio is, how a paper extends it, which distinction needs code and which needs only rules, and what profile enforcement catches that schema validation structurally cannot.

@graph.name: retry-backoff
@graph.title: consulted: reference material nobody performs — a PRINCIPLE, not a procedure: every heading is an argument ("Retrying a definitive answer is not caution", "Jitter is not decoration here"), and it names no actor and no trigger. It is read when writing retry code, never performed as a step.
@graph.description: Every error gets a falling-off retry rate — each wait doubles, with jitter. Read before writing any call that can fail transiently, and before deciding that a failure is worth retrying at all. Exhausting the retries does not change the verdict.

@graph.name: bib-photo-ingestion-watcher
@graph.title: bib-photo-ingestion-watcher
@graph.description: Integration-watcher for bib physical-review issues. When a page photo is uploaded to a `bib-physical-review` issue (or an in-repo source passage is agent-identified), OCR/read it, formalise the cited result (if the project has a formal-proof pipeline), confirm the project's usage matches the source, run machine + agent bib validation, then set the reference status to `validated` and refresh references.review.json. Use when processing a bib-physical-review issue that has an attached photo, or when ingesting an uploaded paper.

@graph.name: harness-requirements
@graph.title: Harness requirements — what an instance owes for what it declares
@graph.description: What an instance OWES for every directory it declares — a visualiser, a documentation entry, a governing skill, json/jsonld/schema.json serialisations at the directory's URL and at every node beneath it, and a starting README of its own. Read before declaring a directory, before adding a graph kind, and when reading `check:subgraph-coverage`. Carries which obligations are ranked as unmet promises rather than unanswered questions, why the discriminator is "is this the static knowledge graph", and which single obligation a harness may never waive.

@graph.name: library-ingestion
@graph.title: Library ingestion
@graph.description: Taking a file from `uploads/` to `library/<bib-slug>/` — which rung to reach for and why, what a complete L1 entry holds, and why an inferred structure is refused rather than guessed. One entry point: `bun run ingest`.

@graph.name: review-heatmap
@graph.title: Review heat map — where to look first
@graph.description: The review page's heat map: a section-by-metric table that tells a reviewer of a large document where to look first. Says what each column MEANS and what it must NOT be read as, where each number comes from, what a column says when a build lacks its data, and how the colour was chosen. Use when a reviewer or author asks "where do I start", reads a number off the heat map, or asks why coverage or QA say "no data"; and before adding a column.

@graph.name: devils-advocate-watcher
@graph.title: /devils-advocate-watcher
@graph.description: Logical devil's-advocate integration watcher — for every content block (.ts/.md) and formal sibling, constructs the strongest adversarial case that it is WRONG: the objection a hostile-but- competent referee would raise (false claim, vacuity, circularity, overclaim, hidden degree-of-freedom, logical non-sequitur, formal↔narrative divergence, citation misuse, definitional ambiguity, empirical fragility, domain implausibility, irreproducible compute). Fans out multiple adversarial-lens agents per block, then an adjudicator scores whether each objection survives rebuttal. Persists per-block <block>.qa.json entries under the `da-*` criteria family (reviewer.kind = "agent"). Operationalizes the standing Critical-distance red-team license (AGENTS.md). Inherits all shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake) from `integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: kg-export
@graph.title: KG export — publishing the graph as linked data, not as a page
@graph.description: Serialize an instance's knowledge graph to one JSON document, for publication and inspection. Read when asked to visualize, audit or share the KG, and before adding a node type to the export.

@graph.name: publish-verification
@graph.title: Publish verification, and the one alert
@graph.description: Verify what a publish produced BEFORE it is deployed, and alert the publication manager whenever any step after the publish button fails — the verifier set, how to add a verifier, what is in scope, and how the publication manager triages the one alert.

@graph.name: interaction-modality
@graph.title: /interaction-modality — ask in a form the person can answer
@graph.description: Establish how to talk to the person in front of you before deciding what to say — audio, ordinary chat, selectable options for limited hand function, large-type for low vision, plain language — and hold that choice durably so every later session and sibling agent honours it. Covers the accessibility rules a conversational agent can actually keep, the settings surface in the published site, and how to drive a question set from DMN so the SAME logic serves every modality. Use at first contact with a new user, when a user reports difficulty answering, whenever a question is about to be asked, and before any long free-text prompt.

@graph.name: one-voice-integration-watcher
@graph.title: /one-voice-integration-watcher
@graph.description: One-voice integration watcher — watches origin/main + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for content-block changes (`.md`, `.ts`, proof files), runs the per-block QA suite covering scholarly voice, AI-slop detection, section/chapter fit, canonical-vs-deprecated notation usage, and domain-boundary placement. Persists every finding to a sibling `<block>.qa.json` audit report (multi-reviewer, per-field SHA staleness). The watcher NEVER stops — when no events arrive it falls back to idle-sweep of the staleness backlog, rebuilding the audit knowledge base that feeds future content reviews. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake, sibling-PR comment protocol) from `local/integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: bean-coordination
@graph.title: Bean Coordination
@graph.description: Pointer to the bean-based session work-plan system (the `beans` CLI flat-file issue tracker, data under `beans/`). Operational usage lives in todo-manager.md / session-intent.md; the generic coordinator/orchestrator logic is owned by the folio-assistant platform.

@graph.name: watch
@graph.title: /watch — background watcher with integration check
@graph.description: Background-watch a branch (default origin/main) or a GitHub PR for new activity while you work, and on every event report whether to integrate / whether it conflicts with the current branch / whether it lets you simplify exposition / proofs / computations

@graph.name: bib-human-review
@graph.title: bib-human-review
@graph.description: Human-validated bibliography workflow. Flag references that have not been human-reviewed against their source; drive the acquisition ladder (source-in-repo → acquire-legally → physical-library); open one GitHub issue per reference needing physical review (full project context + bibliographic data + page-photo request, assigned to the repo owner); hand off uploaded photos to the bib-photo-ingestion watcher. Use when auditing bib human-review status, ingesting an uploaded paper's results, or preparing a physical-review issue.

@graph.name: board-diagram-interchange
@graph.title: Relationship first, visualisation later
@graph.description: A board is a DIAGRAM OF a folio, not a container of one. The OMG split between the semantic model and its layout, why the arrow runs one way, and what a note may never carry.

@graph.name: swarm-management
@graph.title: Swarm management
@graph.description: Decide whether to run parallel agents at all, and if so how many, at which model level, against which decomposition. Read BEFORE dispatching more than one background agent — a swarm spends the author's tokens and the decision is theirs.

@graph.name: integration-watcher
@graph.title: integration-watcher (abstract parent)
@graph.description: Abstract parent skill for domain-specific **integration watchers**. Encodes the shared mechanics — Monitor on `origin/main`, PR subscriptions, per-event QA dispatch, queue + ledger, idle backlog sweep, idle author-ask dispatcher, watch-PRs-you-prepare protocol, voice-pass on PR diff, witness-drift CI recovery, billing-quick-fail flake handling — that every concrete watcher inherits. Children fill nine domain-specific slots; everything else is shared here.

@graph.name: one-voice-style-guide
@graph.title: One-Voice Style Guide — Author Voice Profile
@graph.description: Author voice profile and narrative style guide. Reference when authoring or editing prose. Pairs with `one-voice-audit` (mechanical sweep for status leaks, emoji, and Unicode crashes).

@graph.name: voice-overlay-review
@graph.title: Voice overlay review
@graph.description: Review a block against the active voices' rules and record the verdict on its QA sidecar. The human/agent half of the voice overlay; the mechanical half is whatever `patterns` and `terminology` a rule carries.

@graph.name: integration-backlog
@graph.title: /integration-backlog — drive the backlog to zero, one PR at a time
@graph.description: Dispatcher for the `/integration-backlog <axes>` slash command. Works the backlog identified by the integration watchers (proof, canonical, compute, detangler, one-voice, …) by clustering the open findings into review-sized batches (≤ 49 files per PR — the reviewer-bot limit), proposing each batch to the author via structured AskUserQuestion calls, running `/prepare-merge` on each, resolving review comments (auto if mechanical, structured AskUserQuestion if architectural), then merging — and repeating until the axis is exhausted or the author signals stop. Sister command to `/integration-watch`: the watcher MONITORS for new events; this skill WORKS the backlog the watcher already catalogued.

@graph.name: kg-viewer
@graph.title: Rendering the knowledge graph
@graph.description: Render a published knowledge-graph document so a person can read it — faceted index, node detail, followable edges, and an honest account of what the document is missing. Host-agnostic; the publishing is a separate Tool.

@graph.name: detangler-integration-watcher
@graph.title: /detangler-integration-watcher
@graph.description: Structural-QA integration watcher — watches the default branch + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for organisational changes (paper / chapter manifest edits, new blocks, edited `uses[]` / `kind` / `label` / `interprets` / `defines` / `tags`, block renames) and runs the editor's detanglement skill suite (`content-graph`, `chapter-complexity-review`, `block-density`, `critical-path-analysis`) on every detected change. Queues findings, auto-discharges mechanical fixes (table extraction), routes block reorderings through narrative review before applying them, and escalates section splits / merges / cross-chapter moves / new sections to the author. Inherits shared mechanics from `local/integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: qa-witness
@graph.title: QA witnesses — the published projection of every verdict
@graph.description: The QA projections under `test/results/witnesses/` — what a `qa-witness/v1` document says, which three families produce one, how to read a verdict and the witness behind it, and why "could not determine" is a third state everywhere in them.

@graph.name: instance-kinds
@graph.title: Instance kinds — naming one, and what a new kind must declare
@graph.description: How to make a new KIND of harness instance — choosing the prefix family, the keep-the-kind's-name default and the owner's right to decline it, which inherited files the new owner may repoint, and what a new GRAPH kind must declare. Read before naming a new instance, before adding a value to the graph-kind registry, and before building a visualiser. Carries the test that usually says "this is not a new kind".

@graph.name: literature-search
@graph.title: Literature search — finding the source a citation points at
@graph.description: Finding the source a node cites but does not hold — memory first, then this repository, then open-access services. Always produce a DIRECT download link. Read before recording that a citation cannot be found, and before appraising any source you have not opened. Its central rule: a blocked network is not a missing document, and the two must never share a report.

@graph.name: board-windows
@graph.title: Start in the avatar, open into a window
@graph.description: Everything starts as its avatar; opening projects a window onto the board. The two mechanisms that must not be conflated, z-order, and the fixed chrome a content kind fills in.

@graph.name: skills-and-tools
@graph.title: Skills and Tools — the skill says what, the Tool says how
@graph.description: A skill states a capability generically; a Tool node carries the concrete mechanism. Read before writing or editing any skill, and whenever a skill is about to name a vendor, a CLI, a binary or an API endpoint.

@graph.name: prepare-merge-auto
@graph.title: /prepare-merge-auto — Autonomous merge pipeline
@graph.description: Full autonomous prepare-merge → resolve → merge pipeline. Coordinates with sibling PRs, resolves review comments, asks structured questions only when blocked, then merges.

@graph.name: theme-ui-review
@graph.title: Post-MVP, because there is nothing to check before there is a render
@graph.description: Review what the MVP actually renders — accessibility, branding, languages — once stakeholders have accepted it. Post-MVP by design: there is no role-to-theme mapping to check at build time, so what gets reviewed is the result. Measures rather than asserts, and raises findings rather than fixing them.

@graph.name: uploads-watch
@graph.title: Watching the queue
@graph.description: Notice what has landed in the acquisition queue, and tell an arrival from a backlog. Reports; it never deletes, and never ingests on its own say-so.

@graph.name: todo-manager
@graph.title: Session Task Manager (`beans`)
@graph.description: Maintain and display work-in-progress task lists using the `beans` CLI issue tracker. Track implementation progress, open tasks, missing artifacts, and blocked items across a session.

@graph.name: feature-staging
@graph.title: Feature-branch staging
@graph.description: Manages feature-branch staging deployments under gh-pages/STAGING/<branch-slug>/ for before/after publication review comparison. Handles branch creation, staging deployment, commit SHA stamping, and cleanup.

@graph.name: serving-renderings
@graph.title: Serving a rendering — endpoints, MIME types, and what each host can enforce

@graph.name: data-modelling
@graph.title: Data modelling — the entities, before the fields
@graph.description: Build a data model: identify the entities a body of work is actually about, the relations between them, and the cardinalities — then declare it where the tools can read it. Process-agnostic technique; the CRDM phase that invokes it is `crdm-data-model`.

@graph.name: ui-accessibility
@graph.title: All UI must follow accessibility guidelines
@graph.description: Every user interface this project produces must be operable by keyboard, legible at measured contrast, and comfortable to hit. How to build to that, how to check it, and why an automated pass is not the standard.

@graph.name: delivery-summary
@graph.title: Delivery Summary
@graph.description: Post-delivery summary with server restart command and viewer links

@graph.name: incremental-render
@graph.title: Incremental render — the cache is easy, the cascade is the work
@graph.description: Rendering only what changed — seeding a build from a previous render, the two edges that decide what must re-run, why a step declares GRAPH KINDS rather than paths, and the rule that could-not-determine always re-renders rather than serving a stale page.

@graph.name: vocabulary-authority
@graph.title: Vocabulary authority — one fact, one home, N renderings
@graph.description: One vocabulary is authoritative for one kind of fact, and every other is a derived rendering reached by a declared mapping. Which vocabulary owns what here, the pros and cons behind each ruling, how DC and SKOS overlap and what stops them drifting, and the normalisation-first rule for any modelling or mapping exercise.

@graph.name: surprise-to-corpus
@graph.title: Surprise to corpus — notice it, filter it, then ask
@graph.description: What was unexpected in that task, and does it belong in the corpus? Logical surprise is the detectable kind, recurrence is the filter that stops this generating noise every turn, and the agent PROMPTS — it never writes corpus guidance unasked.

@graph.name: ci-health
@graph.title: CI health — a red workflow looks exactly like a green one from in here
@graph.description: A red workflow looks exactly like a green one from inside a checkout. How to read a default-branch health report, the three verdicts that keep it honest, why a watchdog needs both a session-start print and an unattended run, and the separate external question the Pages deployments need.

@graph.name: adjudication
@graph.title: Adjudication — judgement, when the mechanism ran out of facts
@graph.description: Settle a review that reached no mechanical or consensus agreement. What makes a disagreement adjudicable, the shape seven implementations here already share, why the adjudication LEADS the criterion while the checker's entry is kept beneath it, and the dispensation that records the reason — scoped to a version, never precedent.

@graph.name: methodology-adoption
@graph.title: Adopting a methodology, and choosing between them
@graph.description: How a named external methodology enters the knowledge graph, and how an agent picks which one applies. Read before following a judgement method, before adopting a new one, and before writing a house method instead of adopting one.

@graph.name: code-node-review
@graph.title: Code node review
@graph.description: Review the knowledge graph's CODE nodes — Tool definitions in the `tools` graph and schema definition nodes under `schemas/` — for the joins a reader cannot see: that a node declares what it is, that what it names resolves, and that the mechanism it describes is the one that actually runs.

@graph.name: pending-show
@graph.title: /pending-show — what is this session working on?
@graph.description: Show the current session's pending work — beans list + ledger intent. Read-only.

@graph.name: render-logging
@graph.title: Render logging — the publish branch keeps its own history
@graph.description: Log every render to the publish branch — what was published, removed, restored or deliberately retained — to an append-only log that lives beside what it describes. Use when adding or removing anything on `gh-pages`, when asking "what happened to this preview", or before writing a workflow step that deletes a published artefact.

@graph.name: harness-tiles
@graph.title: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
@graph.description: A tile is a function of the harness watching a directory, not of nodes. Where the tile set comes from, what a tile opens, and the two gaps it reports rather than hides.

@graph.name: uses-editorial-review
@graph.title: `uses[]` Editorial Review
@graph.description: Adjudicate `uses-editorial-completeness` — read a block as a reader would and judge whether its `uses[]` is complete and genuinely expository.  The human/agent half of the `uses` QA axis; the mechanical half runs in `qa-checkers-uses.ts`.

@graph.name: corpus-grep
@graph.title: Corpus-Grep Skill
@graph.description: Pre-declaration corpus check. Before declaring any item "open", "gap", "TODO", "open problem", "pending derivation" — or asserting in chat that something is unresolved in the corpus — run the four-path grep checklist. A source file's `## Status` note lags the corpus by weeks; the corpus is the source of truth. An item is open only after all four paths come back empty (modulo the originating file itself).

@graph.name: symbiotic-interaction
@graph.title: symbiotic-interaction — the three registers of author input
@graph.description: Recognize and respond to the three epistemic registers of author input — Socratic steer (known-answer correction), honest gap (flagged unknown), and intuition seed (tenuous cross-domain identification) — with the coactive-learning measurement spec (per-arc correction quality and turns-to-convergence) and the prompt-lexicon convention. Carries the STRICT rule that a steer correcting a RULE is written into the skill that governs it, in the same turn, quoted and dated — use whenever the author corrects, settles or overrules anything. Generic folio-assistant platform skill.

@graph.name: canonical-watcher
@graph.title: /canonical-watcher
@graph.description: Derivation-discipline integration watcher — watches the default branch + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for non-canonical empirical / fitting / calibration inputs beyond the project's declared set, numerology, or justification/rationalization in place of derivation. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake, post-completion one-voice, sibling-PR comment protocol, backlog-found PR spin-up, handover docs) from `local/integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: prepare-merge
@graph.title: Prepare-merge — get a feature branch ready to land

@graph.name: review-comments
@graph.title: Review comments — from a PR comment to a structured todo
@graph.description: Reviewer comments on a folio's edit-set, from a tagged pull-request comment to a structured todo on the review page. Covers the tag a reviewer types, how the comments are ingested into `folio-review-comment/v1` todos, where the published `review-comments.json` comes from and when it refreshes, how a comment follows a renamed block and survives a removed one, who may change a comment's status, and how to change this process. Use when a reviewer asks how to comment on a block, when the review page shows no comments or a wrong one, when editing the ingestion, or when a folio's staging workflow is set up.

@graph.name: kg-contribution-offer
@graph.title: Offering the knowledge graph — the question nobody was asking
@graph.description: Ask whether agreed requirements should become knowledge-graph content, and as what — in a form the person can answer by selecting. Use at the end of CRDM sign-off, or whenever a body of agreed work could become a skill, a process, a schema or a bean and nobody has been asked. Offers "none" as a first-class answer.

@graph.name: integration-watch
@graph.title: /integration-watch — dispatcher for the integration watchers
@graph.description: Dispatcher for the `/integration-watch` slash command. Routes to one or more of the concrete integration watchers / audits (proof, canonical, compute, detangler, one-voice, consolidation, bibliography, devils-advocate, …). With no argument, lists the available watchers and asks the user which to invoke. With arguments, dispatches the named watchers in parallel (each gets its own Monitor, queue, ledger, and PR-subscription set).

@graph.name: evidence-review
@graph.title: Evidence review — the same rule, a second instance
@graph.description: Evidence review as an instance of untainted verification — the separation of the appraising party from the drafting party, what recurring surveillance in a living guideline shares with a stale QA verdict, and which of guideline methodology's rules are fenced rather than shipped.

@graph.name: archiving-arxiv
@graph.title: Materializing from arXiv
@graph.description: Materializing a paper from arXiv — why the version suffix is part of the identity rather than a detail, what to keep beside the PDF, and which facts must be read from the published API rather than recalled.

@graph.name: mcp-contract
@graph.title: MCP contract — the projected service must match what it was projected from
@graph.description: Verify an MCP service's tools against the Tool nodes and skill declarations they came from — I/O equivalence in both directions. Read before shipping a projected server, and when a tool call fails with an argument the schema said was fine.

@graph.name: diff
@graph.title: Diff — Content Block Change Report
@graph.description: Show per-block content changes with viewer links, changelog, and undo impact analysis

@graph.name: generalise-the-fix
@graph.title: Generalise the fix, then attack the generalisation
@graph.description: You have a fix. Before it ships, ask what CLASS of defect it belongs to and whether the fix sits at the right layer — then attack your own answer: name what the fix now catches that the bug did not. Two axes go wrong, SCOPE and STATE, and widening either past the problem is how a fix becomes the next defect. Applies to a bug fix, a schema change, a detector, or a claim in a paper. Use after the fix works and before the pull request.

@graph.name: ontologist
@graph.title: Semantic Ontologist (Ambiguity Detection & Glossary)
@graph.description: Semantic Ontologist — scans narrative text for ambiguous terms, generates a formal glossary/registry, and produces a mapping linking narrative strings to formal identifiers. Acts as the "Gatekeeper" ensuring every term has a unique type/identity assignment before formalization proceeds.

@graph.name: directory-conventions
@graph.title: Directory conventions — what an instance declares it scans

@graph.name: activity-log
@graph.title: Activity log — what an agent did, kept out of the graph

@graph.name: placement
@graph.title: Placement — decide where it goes before you write it
@graph.description: Establish where a new node belongs BEFORE you create it — which instance, which declared graph, which kind of node, and which of the two "stub" conventions applies. Read before adding a skill, role, actor, workflow, decision table, schema, tool or content object, and before writing any literal that names one folio.

@graph.name: role-model
@graph.title: Roles are swimlanes
@graph.description: Actors, roles and skills — who performs a BPMN task, under which swimlane, with which skills. How a role's skill set is resolved through `inherits` and through a subprocess call chain, how a lane binds to a declared role, and how `kg:audit` finds a dangling skill, lane, role or decision.

@graph.name: task-authorization
@graph.title: Task authorization — four questions before every task
@graph.description: The check every BPMN task execution runs before anything is recorded: is the actor authenticated, assigned to the role the lane binds, authorized by an ODRL policy to perform the task, and allowed access to the content it acts on? One generic check in the engine rather than a step drawn in some diagrams; advisory today, and what would make it strict. Also how the HTTP routes ask the same policies. Triggers on: may this actor, who may perform, authorization, authentication, access rights, permission check, RBAC, rbac.ts, workflow_complete refused, not eligible for role.

@graph.name: archiving-web-pages
@graph.title: Archiving a web page
@graph.description: Capturing a web page so it can be cited later — the two fidelities, what each one is evidence of, and why capturing only one of them loses something that cannot be recovered. A URL is not an archive.

@graph.name: compute-integration-watcher
@graph.title: Compute Integration Watcher
@graph.description: Cross-layer wiring auditor — watches for newly-landed formal/analytic improvements (proofs, propositions, lemmas, axiom→theorem upgrades, witness data) on the default branch AND on open PRs, and checks whether each one has been wired into the production compute chain. Complements `local/compute-audit` (which scans for performance/correctness antipatterns inside scripts). Runs in two modes: REACTIVE (watch new commits / PR events) and IDLE-SWEEP (walk all existing content blocks and audit wiring).

@graph.name: asset-extraction
@graph.title: Asset extraction — the index goes in, the contents do not
@graph.description: Reading a container — a zip, a PDF, a saved web page — into the knowledge graph. What goes in by default (metadata), what does not (contents), the three timestamps that sit near each other and mean different things, and why a producer string is evidence.

@graph.name: code-lists
@graph.title: Code lists
@graph.description: Author, extend or consume a code list: a closed set of codes, each with a label, a definition and a source, kept as a node and published as SKOS. Use when a diagram, a schema or a script needs a fixed set of values (adjudication answers, namespace IRIs) instead of strings in code.

@graph.name: voice-authoring-guidance
@graph.title: Voice authoring guidance
@graph.description: Load the active voices' rules BEFORE writing, so a block is drafted in the register it will be reviewed against. The authoring half of the voice overlay; `voice-overlay-review` is the half that runs after.

@graph.name: bean-blocking
@graph.title: Blocking is a claim about the work, not a mood
@graph.description: Default to non-blocking when updating a bean's status. Mark blocked only when the work genuinely cannot proceed, and then always with what it waits on, when the wait expires, and what the next agent should do.

@graph.name: rendered-verification
@graph.title: /rendered-verification — look at it, then send the picture
@graph.description: Confirm a UI change by LOOKING at it in a browser and sending the screenshots to the author, rather than describing it. Use whenever a change touches CSS, a Liquid/HTML template, a generated page, the navbar, a board, a sticky or any rendered surface — before claiming it works, and before asking the author to review it. Covers building the site locally, taking the REAL CI build off `gh-pages` when the question is theme chrome or layout, driving it with Playwright in this environment, measuring computed style rather than reading the stylesheet, hit-testing a control's centre because visible is not usable, asserting the conditions so a check cannot pass over an unstyled page, and the defect classes that are invisible to a green gate set.

@graph.name: unverified-constraints
@graph.title: consulted: reference material nobody performs — a DISCIPLINE. "Never encode a constraint you have not verified" is a rule that governs other work; its headings are the argument and the worked case. Nobody performs it as a task.
@graph.description: Never encode a constraint you have not verified — a rule that refuses a working setup is worse than no rule. Read before adding a check to a schema, a validator, a gate or an incompatibility table, and whenever you are about to write down that something "is not supported".

@graph.name: turn-reporting
@graph.title: Turn reporting — say which bean you are on, every turn
@graph.description: Say which bean you are on, every turn — the opening and closing report formats, the rules that make a report worth reading (two sentences and a link per bean, every mention), and the STRICT rule that the "next" line is a question and must carry its own context.

@graph.name: deletion-requires-confirmation
@graph.title: Deletion requires explicit confirmation
@graph.description: An agent never removes a durable artefact on its own initiative. Report what would go, with sizes and ages, and wait for the user to say so. Covers what counts as durable, the non-destructive move for each kind, and the rule that a workflow whose shape deletes something counts as a deletion nobody decided.

@graph.name: upstream-version-adoption
@graph.title: Adopting an upstream version bump
@graph.description: Watch a pinned upstream dependency for a new release, and take a candidate version through impact analysis, an MVP build, review and a person's adopt/hold/decline decision. Reusable per pin — the theme is the first tenant, not the only one.

@graph.name: content-graph
@graph.title: Content Graph — Editorial Organisation Skill
@graph.description: Editorial graph analysis skill — builds a content graph from uses[], interprets, proofs, and examples relationships; builds a chapter/section topology graph; and applies heuristics to identify forward references, cross-section/cross-chapter coupling, and sections that are too sparse or too dense. Produces actionable reorganisation suggestions and can implement approved moves.

@graph.name: readme-sections
@graph.title: A folio's README — the folio owns the file, the platform owns the markers
@graph.description: A folio's README is the author's file; the platform owns only the marked regions it generates. How the sync/audit split works, why the whole-file generator it replaced could not, and the third state both tools must report.

@graph.name: decision-audit
@graph.title: A decision is not a finding, and neither is a substitute for the other
@graph.description: Record why a decision was made, or why a finding in it was left. Required of whoever adjudicates a gate, and of the agent that assembles the citations for them. Every overrule of a mechanical finding carries a note, and every note cites corpus evidence.

@graph.name: adopt-methodology-from-source
@graph.title: Adopt a methodology from a source document
@graph.description: The general process for turning a shared paper, book or standard into an adopted methodology: establish origin and licence, ingest the source, find and summarize related beans and issues and ask whether to coordinate, render the method with its adopted and refused parts, place it by ownership, integrate it by calling existing processes, give every tool it uses a Tool node, and put it to the owner. Process: processes/methodology-from-source.bpmn.

@graph.name: idle-backlog
@graph.title: idle-backlog
@graph.description: While idle or waiting on a long-running async task (a build, a long compute script, a CI run, a background agent), pull the applicable backlog in priority order and work non-conflicting items instead of stalling. Generalises AGENTS.md's 5-minute idle trigger into a reusable skill. Use whenever blocked on an async wait with no substantive output to produce.

@graph.name: visual-diff
@graph.title: Visual diff — see a figure change
@graph.description: Pictures of a changed figure, diagram or table, before and after, and how much of it changed. Says when to use it, what the percentage means and must NOT be read as, what a missing picture means, and how the staging job and the review process call it. Use when a reviewer asks "what does this figure look like now", when a table's markup diff is unreadable, or when a staging preview's pictures are missing.

@graph.name: github-state-inspection
@graph.title: Reading GitHub state — resolve the ref, do not compose the URL
@graph.description: Answer questions about GitHub-hosted state — is a page published, where does it live, did CI pass, does a branch exist — by reading the ref or the API, never by composing a URL or fetching one. The first check for any deployment or 404 question is `git ls-tree` of the publish ref.

@graph.name: flushable-containers
@graph.title: Flushable containers
@graph.description: A flushable container is a named store that accumulates by design — a trash you can recover from, a review preview, a console log. It declares a buffer limit, badges when over it, and offers three flush actions: flush all, trim to limit, and select to prune. What "flush" means, and which end of the order is expendable, are declared per container and differ.

@graph.name: continual-progress
@graph.title: /continual-progress — trackable, always-PR'd, continually-committed work
@graph.description: Make in-flight work trackable by others in real time — open a PR from the first commit, push small coherent increments continuously (never hoard uncommitted work), keep a live status checklist in the PR body, and post brief intent on the PR + any overlapping sibling PRs. Use on any multi-step or long-running task, especially when siblings/agents or the author may need to follow, cherry-pick, or take over mid-flight.

@graph.name: untrusted-input
@graph.title: Untrusted input — the value must never become program text
@graph.description: Keep attacker-controlled values out of program text — in GitHub Actions, in command lines, in anything that is parsed before it runs. Read before interpolating any value into a script, and before giving a Tool a command-line input.

@graph.description: Convert abstract `holds : Prop` / `claim : Prop` placeholder Lean stubs into typed sub-claim contexts with manuscript-semantic field names.
