@graph.name: definition-clarity-audit
@graph.title: definition-clarity-audit
@graph.description: Definition / statement clarity + concision audit. A content block can validate (schema-clean, refs resolve, formal-proof sibling present) and still read badly: the defined term is never emphasised, the definition is buried under paragraphs of motivation, or one `definition` block silently bundles three or four distinct definienda. No existing QA axis (voice / structure / bib / proof / …) measures clarity of the statement itself. Use when asked to "bold defined terms", "tighten definitions", "no rambling definitions", "one definition per block", "tight theorem/proposition/lemma statements", or to set up / run a clarity audit. Also runs the inverse audit — a non-`definition` block that secretly carries a definition (`clarity-defn-misplaced`) — plus a statement-purity check (`clarity-stmt-pure`: a theorem/prop/lemma/conjecture carries only its claim; embedded remark / interpretation moves to a follow-on `remark`) and a register check (`clarity-grad-style`: graduate-level formal-math prose — no contractions, second-person, hype, colloquialism, or emoji). Emits per-block QA sidecar params under the `clarity-*` criteria via `content/pipeline/definition-clarity-audit.ts`.

@graph.name: lean-generation
@graph.title: Lean File Generation
@graph.description: Extract theorem-like objects from LaTeX source and generate corresponding Lean 4 stub files with `sorry` placeholders.  Maintains the proof-objects.json manifest linking LaTeX labels to Lean declarations by doc-gen4 URL.

@graph.name: proof-simplifier
@graph.title: Proof Simplifier
@graph.description: Analyse small clusters (2–4) of connected proofs to find simplifications: shared lemmas, redundant constructions, factored abstractions, or shorter proof paths through the dependency graph.

@graph.name: proof-conciseness
@graph.title: Proof Conciseness
@graph.description: Tighten narrative (human-readable) proofs without changing mathematical content. Targets verbose prose patterns in `.md` proof files — padding phrases, re-explained elementary steps, redundant restatement, long case analyses that collapse into tables. Complements proof-simplifier (Lean tactics) and readability-editing (chapter prose); this skill operates on the proof block's `.md` specifically and preserves every logical step.

@graph.name: lean-cache-restore
@graph.title: Lean cache: the authoring loop
@graph.description: The Lean build loop — restore a warm cache before working, and contribute your build back when done. One command each. A restore is ~2 minutes; a cold Mathlib build is 30-60.

@graph.name: lean-proof-review
@graph.title: Lean Proof Review
@graph.description: Review Lean 4 proofs for correctness, style, and completeness. Tracks review scores from multiple reviewers (human and agentic) in proof-objects.json.  Integrates with the agent-review pipeline.

@graph.name: lean-mathlibext-curator
@graph.title: `MathlibExt` Curator Skill
@graph.description: Curate `<Paper>/MathlibExt.lean` — the staging area for upstream- candidate lemmas (List/sort plumbing, Foldl/foldr at Monoid level, Real-function bridges).  Decide what lives in `MathlibExt` vs inline, and tag candidates with `-- TODO upstream: …`.

@graph.name: lean-environment-setup
@graph.title: Lean Environment Setup
@graph.description: Sets up and troubleshoots the Lean 4 environment for Claude Code sessions. Ensures elan, lake, lean are installed so the paper-assistant MCP's Lean tools are operational. Handles sandboxed/cloud environments where downloads may be restricted.

@graph.name: critical-path-analysis
@graph.title: Critical Path Analysis & Context Review
@graph.description: Analyse the critical path of the paper's argument chain, audit statement and proof contexts (e.g. general vs specialised assumptions), identify blocks that need rewriting, and propose cleanups.  Also covers "statement and proof context review" — classifying each result by whether its statement, proof, or both require specialisation assumptions.

@graph.name: proof-gap-audit
@graph.title: Proof Gap Audit
@graph.description: Audit individual proofs and the network of proofs for gaps. Detects intra-proof gaps (unproved assertions, existence without proof, uniqueness asserted but not shown, hand-waving, missing citations) and inter-proof gaps (missing bridging lemmas, broken chains of implication, unstated propositions needed to tie results together).

@graph.name: proof-triage
@graph.title: Proof Triage & Resolution
@graph.description: Systematically triages and resolves `sorry` stubs across the Lean codebase. Inventories all sorry sites, orders them by dependency, attempts proofs using mathlib/library search, and escalates to a proof writer with similar-lemma suggestions when stuck.

@graph.name: groebner-basis
@graph.title: Gröbner Basis Skill
@graph.description: Compute Gröbner bases and normal forms for (possibly non-commutative) algebraic structures using a CAS (e.g. Singular letterplace) or an instrumented project routine. Reduce words to normal form with step-by-step logging, extract invariants, and emit witness JSON.

@graph.name: q-usage-watcher
@graph.title: /q-usage-watcher
@graph.description: q-usage integration watcher — detects how each content block treats the substrate parameter $q$ (symbolic / generic-R / real-positive / q > 1 / |q| > 1 / unit-circle / root-of-unity / fixed q_0 / n/a) and cross-checks the detected regime vector against the chapter's narrative-expected profile. Emits per-block `<block>.qa.json` sidecars under the `q-usage-*` criteria and a global witness JSON. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake) from `local/integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: category-theory
@graph.title: Category Theory Formalization
@graph.description: Category Theory formalization skill — handles diagram chasing, universal properties, functorial translation, and whiskering in Lean 4.  Integrates with Mathlib's typeclass-centric category theory and provides tactic strategies for commutativity proofs.

@graph.name: proof-exposition-review
@graph.title: Proof Exposition Review
@graph.description: Paper-wide retrospective review of a single proof block. Given the current state of the paper — including all blocks added since the proof was written — suggest simplifications to the statement, proof, or surrounding exposition. Complements proof-simplifier (which operates on 2-4 block local clusters) by considering the full dependency graph and all recently-added content.

@graph.name: rendering-auditor
@graph.title: Rendering Auditor
@graph.description: Multi-pass rendering auditor for content blocks. Validates markdown+TeX syntax, notation consistency, compilation, layout, and visual output across both HTML and PDF pipelines. Used by author agents after edits and as part of QC reports.

@graph.name: lean-witness-audit
@graph.title: Lean Witness Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit computation scripts (typically Python) that produce witness statements for Lean formalization. Verify witnesses are complete, self-documenting, use paper notation, link to a content block, and emit Lean-compatible declarations. Detects staleness via script content hash and git commit SHA.

@graph.name: compute-author
@graph.title: Compute-author skill — read before writing compute code
@graph.description: Pre-work briefing + durable patterns for anyone writing or modifying compute scripts (or the native crates they call). Read this BEFORE you write or change compute code — it covers precision discipline, the native↔script boundary cost, exact-arithmetic choices (big-integer vs big-rational vs arbitrary-precision float), algebraic-preflight requirements before optimization shortcuts, and witness-emission discipline. Sibling to `compute-audit` (post-hoc); this skill is pre-work.

@graph.name: formalizer
@graph.title: Lean 4 Formalizer (Narrative to Proof)
@graph.description: Lean 4 Formalizer — translates the logical skeleton of narrative mathematical proofs into Lean 4 tactic blocks.  Uses the Ontologist's glossary to resolve types, maps narrative proof phrases to Lean tactics, and generates sorry-bridged partial proofs that compile.

@graph.name: lean-proof-vacuity-audit
@graph.title: lean-proof-vacuity-audit
@graph.description: Detect and fix Lean "vacuous proof" anti-patterns — declarations that type-check, are sorry-free and axiom-clean, and whose statement matches the .md, yet carry NO mathematical content (they assume what they claim, conclude something trivially true, or rest on a false premise). These slip past `proof-statement-integrity` (which only checks signature-stability + an axiom sweep), so detection is semantic and agent-checked. Use when auditing Lean for circular / vacuous / trivially-true proofs, after a batch proof-statement-integrity normalization (the batch "wrap the conclusion in a structure field and project it" fix produces these), or when a "theorem" looks too easy. Emits per-block QA sidecar params under the `proof-no-*` criteria.

@graph.name: verify-local-substrate
@graph.title: Verify Anchor Connectivity
@graph.description: Verify that every result block of a designated class traces back to a designated anchor definition through the uses[] dependency graph. Identifies gaps where claims lack a formal connection to the anchor, and suggests fixes.

@graph.name: paper-importer
@graph.title: Paper Importer
@graph.description: Import external papers from PDF, LaTeX, or arXiv into the content object system. Scans for theorems, definitions, propositions, lemmas, and other formal environments. Generates .ts manifests and .md content files, optionally creates .lean stubs with sorry-bridged proofs citing the original source. Integrates with proof-writer skills so imported theorems can inform and accelerate formalization of the main paper.

@graph.name: compute-audit
@graph.title: Compute Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit compute scripts for a catalogue of correctness and performance antipatterns extracted from a long review of the project's compute history. Distinguishes CORRECTNESS antipatterns from PERFORMANCE antipatterns. Produces a ranked workplan citing concrete files+lines.

@graph.name: lean-formal-graph
@graph.title: Lean formal dependency graph
@graph.description: Build and query the FORMAL dependency graph — what a proof actually invokes, derived from `lean.ref`. Distinct from `uses[]`, which is editorial. Use for impact analysis, exposition gaps, and declaration ownership.

@graph.name: build-docs
@graph.title: /build-docs
@graph.description: Builds the Lean HTML documentation (doc-gen4) locally in the workspace, for any paper folio's Lean package.

@graph.name: semantic-review-scoping
@graph.title: Semantic review scoping
@graph.description: Decide what to review FIRST. Computes which blocks' semantic correctness can actually affect a target theorem, so agent-adjudicated criteria are spent where they matter instead of swept in file order.

@graph.name: build-pdf
@graph.title: /build-pdf
@graph.description: Builds a paper folio's PDF locally in the workspace — the monolithic PDF plus split per-chapter PDFs.

@graph.name: remark-audit
@graph.title: Remark Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit remarks for provable content. Every remark must interpret a mathematical statement that can be formalized in Lean. Detects dangling remarks (no `interprets` link), ambiguous domain terms, and missing formalization.

@graph.name: proof-integration-watcher
@graph.title: /proof-integration-watcher
@graph.description: Proof-QA integration watcher — watches origin/main + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for narrative-proof (`.md`) or Lean-proof (`.lean`) changes, runs the proof QA skill suite on every detected change, queues gaps, attempts auto-discharge for easy sorries / naked conjectures with provable scaffolding, and escalates the rest to the author. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake, post-completion one-voice, sibling-PR comment protocol) from `local/integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: lean-build-fix
@graph.title: Lean Build Fix Skill
@graph.description: Iteratively fix Lean build errors and linter warnings until the build passes cleanly. Uses MCP diagnostics when available, falls back to parsing lake build output.

@graph.name: proof-editor
@graph.title: Proof Editor (Coordinator)
@graph.description: Coordinator skill for proof review and repair. Runs the full proof skill suite (gap audit, lean review, completeness, simplifier, triage), deduplicates findings across reviewers, ranks by severity and dependency order, and delivers a single author-ready action plan with concrete suggested edits (never applying them without author approval).

@graph.name: chapter-analysis
@graph.title: Chapter Analysis & Formalization
@graph.description: Thorough analysis and Lean 4 formalization of a single manuscript chapter. Extracts all narrative definitions/propositions (excluding remarks), identifies missing glossary terms, writes comprehensive Lean stubs using mathlib, and proves limiting-case and structural theorems where possible.

@graph.name: proof-status-tracking
@graph.title: Proof Status Tracking
@graph.description: Maintain the proof-objects.json manifest tracking formalization status, review records, and LaTeX-to-Lean linkages.  Generate status dashboards and enforce review policies.

@graph.name: rendering-fixes
@graph.title: Rendering Fixes
@graph.description: Quick-fix reference for common rendering errors found by the rendering-auditor. Agents should consult this when editing content blocks to avoid introducing issues and to fix flagged problems efficiently.

@graph.name: simulator-math-audit
@graph.title: Simulator Math Audit
@graph.description: Audit simulator content objects against the formal mathematics they visualise — formulas and physical constants must be derived from the paper's canonical sources, never hardcoded in the visualisation.

@graph.name: proof-narrative-lean-equivalence
@graph.title: Proof Narrative ↔ Lean Equivalence Audit
@graph.description: For each content block with both a narrative proof (.md) and a Lean sibling (.lean), verify the two prove the same thing. Detect stub-weakening (Lean claims less than the paper), overreach (Lean claims more than the paper), hypothesis mismatches, and notation drift. Produces a structured equivalence report; no edits.

@graph.name: proposition-consolidation-audit
@graph.title: /proposition-consolidation-audit
@graph.description: Scan a chapter (or the whole paper) for propositions/theorems/lemmas that overlap structurally — same boxed equation under different parametrisations, near-identical proof skeletons, explicit "specialisation of"/"case of"/"corollary of" wording in `.md`, or high-overlap on (uses, cites, tags). Reports candidates for consolidation: parent → corollary, true duplicates, mergeable statements. Run after large-scale chapter work or when the user notices the exposition has accreted special cases.

@graph.name: document-intake
@graph.title: Document Intake
@graph.description: Process uploaded documents (PDFs, scans, LaTeX, structured/normative guidelines, etc.) from uploads/ into structured content objects. Handles OCR extraction, environment detection, structural analysis, and content-object generation. Supports multi-stage pipelines: raw upload → extracted text → structured blocks → .ts/.md content objects.

@graph.name: ffi-roundtrip-audit
@graph.title: FFI roundtrip audit
@graph.description: Audit compute scripts for script ↔ native ping-pong patterns — loops that cross the FFI / subprocess boundary per iteration, instead of one boundary crossing for the whole pipeline. Each occurrence forfeits a meaningful fraction of wall time to marshalling + script-side combine overhead. Performance-only — no correctness change.

@graph.name: latex-build-cache
@graph.title: LaTeX build performance — findings + what's safe
@graph.description: LaTeX build performance — findings + what's safe. The headline goal was to cache a large multi-chapter `report` build (a ~35-chapter / ~2900-block `report` with a heavy `pgf`/`tikz`/`tikz-cd`/`hyperref` preamble + many tikz-cd diagrams). Both standard caching mechanisms were tested on a real engine and FAILED on this toolchain (see §Negative results), so there is currently NO preamble/diagram cache. What DOES work: getting a TeX engine into the sandbox (`scripts/install-tex.sh`) and quick changed-chapter feature builds (`scripts/feature-build.sh`). Read this BEFORE re-attempting a LaTeX cache so you don't re-walk the rakes.

@graph.name: lean-completeness-audit
@graph.title: Lean Completeness Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit Lean formalization completeness across all papers: verify Lake project setup, check import coverage, identify missing .lean files for content blocks that require them, report formalization gaps, and detect stale witnesses.

@graph.name: content-block-review
@graph.title: Content Block Review
@graph.description: Reviews existing content blocks for adherence to all requirements — structural integrity, Lean proof rules, cross-reference consistency, status accuracy, and naming conventions. Flags violations with actionable diagnostics.

@graph.name: raci
@graph.title: RACI — involvement, over the graph that already exists
@graph.description: RACI over this repository's processes — who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for each activity. Three declared edge kinds over the roles and BPMN activities that already exist, not a new party registry. Use it to work out involvement when a project is initiated, and to sketch its breakdown.

@graph.name: process-state
@graph.title: Process state — the task you are in, inside the process you are running
@graph.description: Track where you are inside a running process — which task, in which swimlane, under which role — and recover deliberately when you find yourself outside it. Read before completing a workflow step, and whenever something unexpected interrupts one. Covers what to do about notes and stickies you re-anchored while off-process, which leave no trace in the artefact.

@graph.name: session-state-machine
@graph.title: Playing a state machine
@graph.description: An agent PLAYING a state machine rather than an engine executing one. Where the non-determinism actually lives, why the diagram stays strict, the `folio:judgement` marker that makes a judgement point countable, and what the machine must never do on the actor's behalf.

@graph.name: bpmn-processes
@graph.title: Processes are BPMN, and the diagrams are executable
@graph.description: Every process here is BPMN, the diagrams are executable, and the base processes are strict. How to author one, how to run it, how a package relaxes a step and what it may never relax, and which gateways are computed rather than chosen.

@graph.name: workflow-state
@graph.title: State in a running process
@graph.description: Where a running process keeps what it knows, and which store answers which question. The three records a step may touch, the one it may not, what `<folio:bean op>` actually performs, and why an instance and a bean must be one answer rather than two.

@graph.name: deterministic-and-agentic
@graph.title: The deterministic-to-agentic spectrum
@graph.description: Workflow processing is a SPECTRUM, not a switch. The four mechanisms this repository already uses to sit at different points on it, the four axes an answer has to name, what is measured today, and the three research questions — which are open, and marked as open.

@graph.name: session-context
@graph.title: Session context
@graph.description: What a state machine tracks across a session, as against one process instance. The six fields, why `actor` is required and the rest are not, why the session's view of a node is advisory, and what a sibling session reads it for.

@graph.name: specification-compiled-agents
@graph.title: Specification-compiled agents
@graph.description: When a diagram already says what the process is, the model should not be planning it. The two gaps between this repository's engine and a compiled control plane — typed node contracts and per-node context scope — what to do before either exists, and the three things not to adopt with the method.

@graph.name: deep-document-research
@graph.title: Deep document research
@graph.description: Answer a question from a corpus this folio already holds, iteratively, and stop on a stated condition. The four roles, the two stopping conditions and why both are load-bearing, the granularity choice, and the three things this repository must NOT adopt along with the method.

@graph.name: materialize-remote
@graph.title: Materializing remote content
@graph.description: Landing remote content locally — the five gates, the three states, and the two purposes. One process, shared by catalogue import and harness bootstrap, plus the refresh that is not a re-import.

@graph.name: materialize-on-demand
@graph.title: Materialize on demand
@graph.description: After bootstrap, a person asks for part of a remote subgraph to be held locally. Check what is already here (cache:index), put a number on the ask before anything is fetched, then run materialize-remote. Eviction is a report, never an act.

@graph.name: copy-out-materialized
@graph.title: Working on materialized content — copy it out
@graph.description: Materialized content is read-only. To work on it you take a copy into your own folio/, and the copy records what it is a copy of — the local-provenance edge, which is not the upstream one.

@graph.name: iris-dspace
@graph.title: IRIS, DSpace and Dublin Core
@graph.description: How WHO IRIS uses DSpace and qualified Dublin Core — the three identifier systems, MeSH as a controlled vocabulary, bundles, and the containment path. What a later tool needs from a record, stated as requirements it can be checked against.

@graph.title: Technical Officer
@graph.description: Programme area coordinator and first-pass reviewer who bridges the development team and subject matter experts.

@graph.title: Stakeholder
@graph.description: Signs off that a requirement is met. Holds no capabilities here deliberately: sign-off is a judgement, and a capability would suggest it could be automated.

@graph.title: Board renderer
@graph.description: The client-side code that draws a folio's boards where the reader is: the avatar, window and layout machinery each content kind declares into. Mechanical — it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, which is why every decision in the board diagrams sits in the reader's lane. It is NOT the CI pipeline: that publishes and never reacts to a reader, and conflating the two would put a person's click behind a build.

@graph.title: FHIR Modeller
@graph.description: L3 machine-readable artifact creator who translates L2 specifications into FHIR Implementation Guide artifacts using FSH, SUSHI, CQL, and IG Publisher.

@graph.title: Terminologist
@graph.description: Semantic interoperability and terminology governance specialist who maps data elements to standard terminologies (ICD-11, SNOMED CT, LOINC).

@graph.title: End user
@graph.description: The person the assistant is working for — the one who states intent and answers what the agent cannot decide from the filesystem.

@graph.title: IG Publisher Service
@graph.description: System actor providing FHIR IG Publisher build and QA reporting.

@graph.title: Review Agent
@graph.description: LLM agent performing NON-MECHANICAL validation — accuracy, voice, exposition, whether a change says what the editor meant. Judgement calls escalate to a human reviewer or SME.

@graph.title: Translator
@graph.description: Localization specialist who adapts content for UN-supported languages.

@graph.title: CI health watcher
@graph.description: Reads whether a workflow is actually working on the default branch, and reports it. A mechanical participant in the CI process: it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, so anything needing a decision belongs in another lane. Its three reporting rules are the judgement-free ones — "could not check" is never rendered as green, a red that has not re-run in a week is flagged as possibly stale rather than as an active fire, and a red whose workflow file changed after the failing run is reported superseded. Each is a statement about evidence, not a verdict on what to do about it.

@graph.title: Untainted adjudicator
@graph.description: The dispatched party that rules — given the original intent and the checker's output, and never the artefact itself. It names each drift against the criterion's declared `drift` statement and returns pass / warn / fail. It holds `qa-reporting` and its witness leads the criterion, because the first entry per criterion is the operative one. It does NOT hold `content-authoring`: the party that produced the artefact does not write the verdict on it, which is the whole discipline in one line.

@graph.title: Ingestion engine
@graph.description: Runs unattended over a source corpus. No user is in the room, so every gate it reaches must be decidable from the material itself.

@graph.title: Programme Manager
@graph.description: Overall coordination and governance. Responsible for scope definition, team formation, resource allocation, timeline planning, and stakeholder engagement.

@graph.title: Publication Manager
@graph.description: Release and deployment manager responsible for IG configuration, builds, versioning, publication, and platform updates.

@graph.title: CI pipeline
@graph.description: The build and validation system: validate, render, publish, and the mechanical half of the HCI gate. It runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, so anything needing a decision belongs in another lane.

@graph.title: Attestation service
@graph.description: The signing endpoint. Declares `reach: "internet"` because an API signer that cannot reach out is not a signer — this is the one actor whose reach is part of what it IS, rather than a fact about where it happens to run.

@graph.title: Untainted checker
@graph.description: The dispatched party that renders an artefact independently — a back-translation, an independent finding — given only what `UntaintedDispatch.checker_sees` allows and nothing that would let it shortcut. It RULES ON NOTHING: its witness carries `result: "n/a"` and the intermediate text a reader needs to ask 'on what basis?'. It deliberately does NOT hold `qa-reporting`, and that absence is the point — a checker that emits a verdict is comparing a thing with its own paraphrase of itself, and `check:qa-reviewer-permission` refuses it structurally rather than by convention.

@graph.title: Collaborator (gateway session)
@graph.description: A person signed in through the auth-gateway's GitHub OAuth and listed in deploy/github-collaborators.txt. The gateway's `collaborator` tier as an actor (issue #1207): what it may do over HTTP is cat-harness/policies/http-gateway.jsonld, not a rung compared in code. Takes on no BPMN role; a person who works in a lane does so as the actor that lane's role names.

@graph.title: Owner (gateway session)
@graph.description: The repository owner signed in through the auth-gateway's GitHub OAuth. The gateway's `owner` tier as an actor (issue #1207). Over HTTP it holds exactly what `collaborator` holds, because no route distinguishes them; `commit to main` is GitHub's branch protection, not a route. Its grants are cat-harness/policies/http-gateway.jsonld.

@graph.title: Administrator
@graph.description: Full administrative access. `roles` is what it may act AS and `capabilities` what its machine has. What it may DO is no longer written here: it is an ODRL rule in cat-harness/policies/folio-defaults.jsonld (issue #1180).

@graph.title: Local sweep
@graph.description: The same QA sweep programs as `ci-pipeline`, run on a contributor's or agent's machine rather than in CI. It runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement. It is a SEPARATE actor because the verdict it produces rests on a working tree nobody else can reconstruct: a CI verdict is reproducible from the commit it records, while a local one may rest on an uncommitted edit. Recording which one ruled is what keeps `reviewed_sha` an address rather than a decoration.

@graph.title: Onboarding agent
@graph.description: The authoring agent acting before there is a folio: clarifying what "create a folio" means here, scanning an existing repo, scaffolding, and reporting the published URL only once it answers.

@graph.title: Lean MCP Server
@graph.description: System actor providing Lean 4 proof checking and diagnostics via MCP protocol.

@graph.title: Librarian
@graph.description: Acquires a source and files it. `person` rather than `agent`, and the distinction is load-bearing: the decisions this actor owns are the ones an unattended engine must NOT make on its own — whether a capture may be redistributed, whether a logged-in view counts as the public document, and when an approximate vocabulary term is worse than a local one. An agent performs the capture; a person settles what it means.

@graph.title: Reviewer

The role admits `person` too, and no person-shaped actor is registered for it because none has been named; inventing one would assert a party this repository does not have. WHAT THIS ACTOR MAY NOT DO is report an agent's draft figure description as what the figure shows — `schemas/narrative.ts` holds that line, and it is why an agent performing this is legitimate in the first place. ITS PERMISSION IS IN THE ODRL POLICY, not here: #1186 moved every actor's own `permissions` list into `policies/folio-defaults.jsonld` as an assignee/action rule, and `odrl.test.ts` fails any actor file that still carries one. Reads a change and judges whether a literal names one folio, whether a new content type needs an adapter or only a profile, and whether a node declares what it is. @graph.title: A check that examined nothing does not report a pass

@graph.title: A comment says WHY, and names the measurement
@graph.description: The convention this repository actually follows in code it keeps: a comment records the defect the line prevents and what was measured, not a restatement of the line.
@graph.statement: A comment explains why the code is as it is — the defect it prevents, the alternative that was tried, the number that was measured. Never a paraphrase of what the line already says.
@graph.rationale: This repository's own modules are unusually heavily commented and the comments earn it: `ci-gates.ts` records the 27-of-33 miscount that produced it, `known-skills.ts` records the silent drop. A comment restating the code goes stale invisibly, because nothing contradicts it; a comment naming a measurement can be checked and can be wrong out loud.

@graph.description: Summarise a folio's committed per-block QA verdicts into one `block-qa.json` a staging preview publishes: each block is failing (a FRESH verdict failed, with the worst severity), stale (a verdict predates the block's current files), passing, or unaudited. Freshness is the QA sweep's own rule, including the uses-graph hash for graph-scoped criteria. Runs no checker and writes no verdict.

inputs.name: folio
inputs.description: The folio's `folio` graph directory.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Where to write `block-qa.json`.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: The folio's instance root, where verdicts are anchored. Default: found from `folio` exactly as the QA sweep finds it.

outputs.name: block-qa
outputs.description: A `folio-block-qa-summary/v1` file keyed by block label. Its counts go to stderr.

@graph.name: folio-block-screenshots
@graph.title: Folio block screenshots
@graph.description: Picture each changed figure, diagram, table, equation or simulator block on the published main site and on a staging build, and compare the two pictures pixel by pixel in Chromium's canvas. Writes `visual-diff.json` (`folio-visual-diff/v1`: per block, the share of pixels changed beyond anti-aliasing, and the before, after and diff pictures) and `visual/*.png`, which the review page's visual renderer shows. A side that cannot be pictured (page or anchor missing) is recorded as missing, never drawn blank. Adds no dependency: Playwright is already the platform's browser driver.

inputs.name: changeset
inputs.description: The preview's `changeset.json`: which blocks changed, and their kind on each side.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: The published main site, as a directory (the publish branch's root).

inputs.name: head
inputs.description: The staging build's site directory.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Where to write `visual-diff.json` and `visual/`: the site root, so the review page finds them.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: Print how many changed blocks would be pictured, and stop, so a caller installs a browser only when there is work.

outputs.name: visual-diff
outputs.description: `<out>/visual-diff.json` and `<out>/visual/*.png`. A per-block summary goes to stderr.

inputs.name: askedOf

@graph.name: pdf-cover
@graph.title: PDF page raster
@graph.description: Render one page of a PDF to a PNG — the thumbnail a repository listing shows — and print the provenance a catalogue needs to record it as DERIVED: source, digest, page, geometry, renderer.

inputs.name: out

outputs.name: facts

@graph.name: feature-staging
@graph.title: Stage a branch's preview
@graph.description: Publish a branch's built site to `STAGING/<slug>/` on the publish branch, so a reviewer compares a rendered before and after rather than a description of one. Stamps the commit SHA, and removes the preview when its pull request closes.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.description: The branch to stage; blank stages the current one. On a pull request the workflow fires by itself and needs none of these.

inputs.name: cleanup_slug
inputs.description: DELETION: the `STAGING/<slug>` to remove, instead of staging anything. It exists because the label path cannot reach the previews the health sweep reports — being findable as an orphan REQUIRES the pull request to be closed, so the close event has already fired with no label (bean `w2g5`).

inputs.name: cleanup_confirm
inputs.description: The slug again, exactly. Anything else refuses. A confirmation therefore cannot be carried over from a previous run against a DIFFERENT preview, which a boolean would have allowed.

outputs.name: preview
outputs.description: Where the preview is served. A reviewer cannot assess a rendered artefact from a description of it, which is what this URL is for.

@graph.name: serve-rendering
@graph.title: Local rendering server
@graph.description: Serve an instance's renderings over local HTTP with their declared media types. The publication host wherever GitHub Pages is absent, and the only host that can enforce `application/ld+json` at all.

inputs.name: directory
inputs.description: Tree to serve; defaults to the built site when present.

inputs.name: port
inputs.description: 0 binds a free port, which is what the tests use.

outputs.name: url
outputs.description: Where the tree is being served.

@graph.name: kg-graph-export
@graph.title: Knowledge-graph export
@graph.description: Dump this instance's knowledge graph — skills, BPMN activities and their lanes, roles, actors, directories — to one JSON-LD document for publication. The export is data; something else draws it.

inputs.name: baseUrl
inputs.description: Publication base the node IRIs are minted against; a preview passes its own.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Where to write; defaults to `_kg/<stub>.jsonld`, which is build output and gitignored.

outputs.name: graph
outputs.description: The written JSON-LD document.

outputs.name: problems
outputs.description: Sources that could not be read, counted rather than silently omitted.

@graph.name: qa-sweep
@graph.title: QA sweep
@graph.description: Run every registered criterion over the blocks under a path and write a per-block QA sidecar. A sidecar rather than a console report, because a printed verdict cannot distinguish "never checked" from "checked and clean".

inputs.name: targetPath
inputs.description: The content root to sweep. Absent, the command exits 2 with its usage — could-not-determine, not a clean sweep.

inputs.name: dryRun
inputs.description: Report what would change without writing sidecars.

inputs.name: ci
inputs.description: Fail on a finding rather than recording it.

outputs.name: sidecars
outputs.description: One `<block>.qa.json` per block, committed beside its subject.

@graph.name: latex-preflight
@graph.title: LaTeX preflight
@graph.description: Lint TeX source for the pdflatex-compile failure classes a permissive AST parser accepts — the ones that pass validation and then break the build.

inputs.name: warn
inputs.description: Report without failing — for a corpus not yet clean.

outputs.name: findings
outputs.description: Compile-breaking hazards, located. A clean run here is not a successful compile; it is the absence of these classes.

@graph.name: latex-overfull
@graph.title: LaTeX overfull-box report
@graph.description: Turn a pdflatex log's Overfull \hbox warnings into a located, actionable report, with a threshold so a long tail of trivial overruns does not bury the real ones.

inputs.name: log
inputs.description: The pdflatex log to read. Nothing to read means no answer, not a pass.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Ignore overruns below this size — the long tail is noise, and reporting it hides the rest.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: Fail above this count, for use as a gate.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: Located overfull boxes. Requires a build log: with no log there is nothing to read, which is could-not-determine rather than clean.

@graph.name: lean-build
@graph.title: Lean build
@graph.description: Build every Lean project in the workspace from the root Lake manifest, so cross-package dependencies resolve against it rather than a possibly-stale per-paper manifest. Writes a committable build-status sidecar every run.

inputs.name: paper
inputs.description: Build one paper instead of all of them.

inputs.name: cache
inputs.description: Fetch the Mathlib cache first. A from-source Mathlib build is 30–60 minutes against ~2 for a restore.

inputs.name: update
inputs.description: Run `lake update` before building.

inputs.name: logDir
inputs.description: Where logs and the status sidecar go.

outputs.name: status
outputs.description: `lean-build-status.json` — committable, so a green build is distinguishable from one nobody ran.

@graph.name: lean-cache
@graph.title: Lake olean cache
@graph.description: Restore, verify, seed and diagnose the prebuilt `.lake/` artefacts for a Lean package. Always try `restore` first: a from-source Mathlib build is 30–60 minutes, a restore about two.

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: The verb. `doctor` exists because a restore that silently missed used to look exactly like one that worked.

inputs.name: lakeRoot
inputs.description: The package whose `.lake/` is acted on.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: A real hit, a miss, or a diagnosis — never a miss that reads as a hit.

@graph.name: lean-toolchain-setup
@graph.title: Lean toolchain install
@graph.description: Install the toolchain pinned in `lean-toolchain`, fetching it from the GitHub release rather than through elan's downloader. Idempotent, and it detects partial state rather than re-downloading.

outputs.name: toolchain
outputs.description: The linked toolchain name, and the per-repo override that selects it.

@graph.name: lean-coverage
@graph.title: Lean coverage
@graph.description: Count how many provable blocks — theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary — carry a full Lean proof rather than a sorry, per paper. The completeness half of the Lean audit: what is formalised, and what is still a gap.

inputs.name: paper
inputs.description: One paper instead of all.

inputs.name: contentRoot
inputs.description: Where content blocks live. NOT a Lean project root — see the note above this node.

outputs.name: coverage
outputs.description: Provable blocks, and how many are sorry-free. A count, not a verdict: a sorry-free proof can still be vacuous, which is the sibling node's question.

@graph.name: lean-audit
@graph.title: Lean vacuity audit
@graph.description: Inspect Lean declarations chapter by chapter for proofs that type-check, are sorry-free and axiom-clean, and still carry no mathematical content — assuming what they claim, concluding something trivially true, or resting on a false premise.

inputs.name: chapter
inputs.description: One chapter instead of the whole corpus.

inputs.name: checkAxioms
inputs.description: Axiom-cleanliness is a separate question from vacuity: a proof can be axiom-clean and still assume its conclusion.

outputs.name: findings
outputs.description: Sorry inventory and trivial-truth detections. Sibling of `lean-coverage`, not an alternative to it: that one COUNTS what is proved, this one asks whether a proof says anything.

@graph.name: kg-audit
@graph.title: Knowledge-graph audit
@graph.description: Audit every join in the actor→role→skill→task sentence and write a committed QA sidecar per node. A printed verdict is gone; a sidecar is what makes "unbound since it was drawn" distinguishable from "broken in the commit under review".

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Compare against the committed sidecars and fail on a critical finding or a stale one, instead of writing.

inputs.name: strict
inputs.description: Promote `major` to failing as well. Not what CI runs; see the note on constant-red checks in `remote-skill-servable.test.ts`.

outputs.name: sidecars
outputs.description: The QA tree, mirroring each subject's own path — flat would collide, since several basenames already occur twice.

outputs.name: worstSeverity
outputs.description: critical, major, minor — or none. `unknown` findings are never a pass.

@graph.name: bpmn-render
@graph.title: BPMN diagram rendering
@graph.description: Render each process diagram to SVG for the documentation site. The .bpmn file is the source of truth; the picture is generated from it, so a diagram and its image cannot disagree.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Fail if any committed SVG is stale, instead of writing.

outputs.name: diagrams
outputs.description: The generated SVG directory. Never hand-edited.

@graph.name: wireframe-check
@graph.title: Wireframe check at web and mobile viewports
@graph.description: Render each mid-fidelity wireframe candidate at a web viewport (1280x800) and a mobile viewport (390x844). For each viewport it records `script` entries for renders, no-overflow and no-placeholder, each pass or fail with a note. It writes a screenshot per viewport and a report.json, and exits non-zero on any fail.

inputs.name: candidates
inputs.description: Wireframe HTML files. Each must carry both a web and a mobile layout (responsive CSS or two layouts).

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Where screenshots and report.json go; default .build/wireframes.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: report.json: per candidate, per viewport, per criterion. The screenshots are beside it.

@graph.name: uml-overview
@graph.title: UML overview per named sub-graph
@graph.description: Draw one UML class diagram per harness and one per named sub-graph it declares, as PlantUML and Mermaid from one model, with every class read from the graph kind's node schema, and render the PlantUML to the SVG each page shows (needs Java; the check does not). A kind with none is drawn as could-not-determine, never as an empty box.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Fail if any diagram, SVG or page is stale or orphaned, instead of writing.

outputs.name: diagrams
outputs.description: uml/overview/ (.puml and .mmd), their SVG renderings, and the docs/uml/overview/ pages that show them.

@graph.name: uml-object-model
@graph.title: Harness object model as PlantUML
@graph.description: Draw the harness object model (Actor, Role, Skill, Process, Task, Todo, Bean, tests, schemas) with every attribute read from the schema behind it. Each relationship names the field that carries it, and the generator refuses to write if that field is gone.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Fail if the committed diagram is stale. Needs the beans CLI; without it the result is could-not-check (exit 2).

outputs.name: diagram
outputs.description: The object-model diagram, in the instance's declared uml directory.

@graph.name: content-graph-uml
@graph.title: A paper's block graph as UML
@graph.description: Draw a paper's block graph from buildContentGraph: chapters as packages, editorial edges (uses / interprets) solid and formal Lean edges (type / value) dashed purple, never one derived from the other, and each block filled by its formalization status from proof-objects.json when given. One diagram for the paper and one per chapter, each in portrait and landscape, stamped with its source's hash. Run from a folio: the platform carries no paper.

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: The folio's content directory, where the block manifests are.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Where to write the .puml files and their SVGs.

inputs.name: status
inputs.description: proof-objects.json, for status fills. Without it every block is drawn unfilled.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Fail if a diagram or SVG is stale or orphaned, instead of writing. Needs no Java.

outputs.name: diagrams
outputs.description: content-graph.puml and content-graph/<chapter>.puml, with portrait and landscape SVGs beside them.

@graph.name: themes-css
@graph.title: Theme stylesheet
@graph.description: Render the declared theme nodes into the stylesheet the site serves. The nodes are the source: a colour has one home, and light and dark are two valuations of one token set rather than two hand-kept blocks.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Compare against the committed copy and fail if stale, instead of writing.

outputs.name: stylesheet
outputs.description: The generated stylesheet. Build output that happens to be committed, so it is readable on the forge — never hand-edited.

@graph.name: avatars-css
@graph.title: Avatar stylesheet
@graph.description: Render the declared avatar nodes — an actor's glyph and colours, including the overlay states — into the stylesheet the site serves.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Compare against the committed copy and fail if stale, instead of writing.

outputs.name: stylesheet
outputs.description: The generated stylesheet. Never hand-edited.

@graph.name: schema-docs
@graph.title: Skill contract reference
@graph.description: Render each skill's input/output JSON Schema as a browsable Markdown reference page, with an index. The generated pages are committed so they are readable on the forge as well as on the site.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Compare against the committed pages and fail if stale, instead of writing.

outputs.name: pages
outputs.description: The generated reference directory. Never hand-edited.

@graph.name: skill-docs
@graph.title: Skill instruction reference
@graph.description: Render the skill instruction bodies — the prose an agent actually loads — as browsable pages with an index, so a reader can see what an agent is told without cloning the repository.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Compare against the committed pages and fail if stale, instead of writing.

outputs.name: pages
outputs.description: The generated instruction directory. Never hand-edited.

@graph.name: ns-vocabulary
@graph.title: Namespace vocabulary
@graph.description: Emit the folio namespace as a document that dereferences — one node per class and property, each with an @id, a type, a label and a definition, so a consumer holding only the JSON-LD can resolve any term it meets.

inputs.name: layer
inputs.description: Emit one namespace layer — `bootstrap` for the layer that must resolve before anything else does.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Where to write; defaults under `_kg/`, which is build output.

outputs.name: vocabulary
outputs.description: The written namespace document.

@graph.name: content-context
@graph.title: Content JSON-LD context
@graph.description: Emit the published JSON-LD `@context` that both populations share — authored block siblings and ingested `library/**` nodes reference it by URL — generated from its TypeScript definition rather than hand-kept.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Compare against the committed copy and fail if stale, instead of writing.

outputs.name: context
outputs.description: `ns/content/v1.jsonld`, the document served at CONTENT_CONTEXT_URL.

@graph.name: context-prefixes
@graph.title: JSON-LD prefix check
@graph.description: Check every committed JSON-LD document in both directions: each prefix a context binds is spoken by something (or forward-declared with a reason), each prefix a document SPEAKS as a key or `@type` is bound in its context, each binding onto one of our own namespaces is spelt as that instance's stub, and every plain key in a document on the published content context is a declared term (never descending into an `@json` value). A context it cannot resolve is reported as undetermined, never clean.

inputs.name: json
inputs.description: Emit both reports as JSON instead of the console summary.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: Console (or JSON) report; exit 1 on an unbound prefix, a misspelt own prefix, a silent binding, or an empty corpus.

@graph.name: gates
@graph.title: The platform's quality gates
@graph.description: Run the checks CI runs, derived from the workflow rather than listed here. One Tool for all of them, not one per gate: the list is computed from `.github/workflows/code-quality-gates.yml` at call time, so it cannot drift from what CI actually enforces.

inputs.name: all
inputs.description: Add the jobs that need a browser; the default is the fast set.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: Print the derived gates and exit, running none.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: One line per gate, then a pass count or the failures. Three exit codes, because two cannot carry the distinction: 0 every gate passed, 1 a gate failed, 2 the gate set could NOT BE DERIVED — the workflow it reads is absent or yields nothing. A caller must not read 2 as either verdict; it matters most downstream, where this Tool is inherited and `.github/workflows/` is not.

@graph.name: gates-merged
@graph.title: Gates on the merged tree
@graph.description: Build this branch merged with the current base in a throwaway worktree and run the full `bun run gates` there — the state a merge will actually produce, which neither the branch's CI nor the base's CI evaluates. Exit 0 passes, 1 conflicts or fails, 2 could not determine (never read as clean). The working copy is never touched.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: The base branch to merge with; `main` when omitted. Fetched first.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: The gate report for the merged tree, or the conflicting paths.

@graph.name: narrative-queue
@graph.title: What narratives are waiting on a person
@graph.description: List the agent-drafted narratives awaiting human confirmation, numbered, with the numbered rejection reasons beside them. The queue is the only place a draft's state is visible before someone accepts it.

outputs.name: queue
outputs.description: Every narrative awaiting a person, NUMBERED, with its subject, its text and its file — then the two commands that act on a number, then the rejection reasons, also numbered. Numbered throughout because the person this is for has very limited hand function and every action must be a selection rather than a typed sentence; `interaction-modality`'s `low-dexterity` profile is the general rule.

@graph.name: check-tools
@graph.title: Do the Tool nodes agree with their skills?
@graph.description: Check every Tool node's joins: that each `satisfies` resolves to a real skill and agrees with that skill's declared contract, that every io port names a declared type, and that no argv input has a type able to express a shell payload.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: The satisfies map, the count of skills with and without a Tool, then the verdict. Exit 0 every join holds, 1 at least one does not. A skill with NO Tool is reported and is deliberately NOT a failure — many are pure judgement, and failing on them would make the report unusable.

@graph.name: tool-coverage
@graph.title: Which uncovered skills warrant a Tool?
@graph.description: Triage the skills that have no Tool by EVIDENCE rather than by grep: a serviceTask naming it or an I/O contract puts it in tier A, a userTask only in B, a shell block or a declared script in C, and nothing in D. The answer to "which of these still have their mechanism inlined in their prose".

outputs.name: triage
outputs.description: Four tiers with A, B and C listed by name and their evidence, D as a count. Always exit 0: this REPORTS a judgement queue and never gates — an uncovered skill is not a defect, and failing on one would make stubbing a gap turn CI red.

@graph.name: mcp-capture
@graph.title: What this instance's MCP server serves
@graph.description: Read the real tool surface from the registrars by mounting each against a capture object — the same objects the server asks, so the Zod shapes and their optionality are the served ones rather than a reading of the source.

inputs.name: json
inputs.description: Emit `{tools, problems}` as JSON for a consumer, instead of the table for a reader.

outputs.name: surface
outputs.description: One row per served tool with its module and its required/optional keys. Three exit codes: 0 the surface was captured whole, 2 one or more modules COULD NOT BE READ so the capture is incomplete, and no equivalence verdict may be drawn from it. There is no exit 1 — this tool reports what is served and never judges it.

@graph.name: render-log
@graph.title: Record what the publish branch served
@graph.description: Append one entry to the render log on the publish branch: what was published or taken down, when, from which commit, and — for a removal or a retention — WHY. The log is the only place a preview that vanished leaves a trace.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: A checkout of the publish branch, or a publish directory about to become one. This tool NEVER fetches, commits or pushes: the workflows that call it already hold the checkout with their own retry and concurrency handling, and a second pusher racing those is a new way to lose a deploy.

inputs.name: event
inputs.description: `rendered`, `removed`, `restored` or `retained`. `retained` is the one that makes the log worth reading — a removal CONSIDERED and refused, which otherwise leaves no trace at all.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: What was rendered — `staging-preview`, `site`, `export`. Open on purpose: the publish branch carries more than previews, and a closed enum would put a schema change between somebody and logging what they published.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: The path on the publish branch. Checked as a VALUE, never trusted by provenance: the slug sanitiser can emit `..`, and that is only safe for a slug taken from a git ref — a dispatch input is not one (bean `fuzm`).

inputs.name: slug
inputs.description: The staging slug, where the subject has one.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.description: The branch the render came from.

inputs.name: commit
inputs.description: The commit the artefact was built from.

inputs.name: run
inputs.description: The workflow run that wrote this, so a reader can open the log.

inputs.name: prose
inputs.description: One JSON object on STDIN: `{summary, reason?, detail?, format?}`. `summary` is required and one line. `reason` is required by the SCRIPT for `removed` and `retained` — an entry saying an artefact went and not why is the ambiguity the log exists to prevent. `format` declares how the prose reads (absent means plain text, never sniffed). Build it with `jq -n --arg`, never by concatenation.

outputs.name: entry
outputs.description: The day's JSONL the entry was APPENDED to. Append is the only verb: there is no `--remove`, no `--edit` and no `--id`, so a takedown is a `removed` ENTRY rather than the erasure of the `rendered` one before it — the never-delete rule made structural instead of a guard three cleanup paths have to remember.

@graph.name: ci-health
@graph.title: Is CI passing on the default branch?
@graph.description: Report each workflow's state on the default branch, which a checkout cannot see: a red workflow looks exactly like a green one from in here. One API call over the recent run history, not one request per workflow — fanning out would exhaust the unauthenticated 60/hr limit and make it unusable at session start.

inputs.name: markdown
inputs.description: Emit the block the session-start sweep prints. ALWAYS exits 0, deliberately: the sweep runs it as `if ! …; then` and would otherwise print the report AND declare it unchecked every time CI is red.

inputs.name: warn
inputs.description: Report only, never fail. For a caller that wants the state without a verdict.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Write the markdown report to a file AND keep the exit code — which `--markdown` cannot do, since it always exits 0. The notifier gets its own flag rather than one API call being spent twice.

outputs.name: report

@graph.name: user
@graph.title: User
@graph.description: The person the assistant is working for. States intent, answers the questions the agent cannot decide from the filesystem, and confirms anything irreversible.

@graph.name: author
@graph.title: Author
@graph.description: Writes and revises folio content. The position, not the person: an editor and a guideline developer both act as author when they are changing a block.

@graph.name: editor
@graph.title: Editor
@graph.description: Author plus the authority to accept a change into the corpus. The lane that sees QA findings and decides.

@graph.name: reviewer
@graph.title: Reviewer / SME
@graph.description: Reads a change and judges it. Cannot accept it — that is the editor's lane — and the separation is why review findings are advice rather than commits. The GENERIC review position: what kind of thing changed decides which subprocess it descends into (review-task.bpmn), and the actor takes on that inner lane's role for the call path only.

@graph.name: review-coordinator
@graph.title: Review coordinator
@graph.description: Organises a review without deciding it. Pulls tagged review comments in, splits a large change into slices by section, assigns each slice to a reviewer of the right role, and watches coverage until every changed block has a verdict or a reasoned waiver. Cannot accept or reject: that is the editor's lane, and the separation is the owner's ruling (2026-09-23, bean en2d). Not a reviewer: it does not inherit one, because assigning a slice is not reading it.

@graph.name: narrative-reviewer
@graph.title: Narrative reviewer
@graph.description: Judges PROSE — register and voice, the editorial dependencies a reader needs, and translation. Entered by DESCENDING into Process_NarrativeReview: the actor keeps its outer review role and adds these skills along that call path, rather than every reviewer carrying them everywhere.

@graph.name: code-reviewer
@graph.title: Code reviewer
@graph.description: Judges the knowledge graph's CODE nodes — Tool definitions in the `tools` graph and schema definition nodes under `schemas/`. Not ordinary code review: the question is whether the NODE is sound — does it declare what it is, do its references resolve, is the mechanism it advertises the one that runs — which a passing test suite does not answer. Entered by DESCENDING into Process_CodeReview.

@graph.name: qc-reviewer
@graph.title: QC reviewer
@graph.description: Reviewer with the publication quality gate. Checks the built artefact, not only the source.

@graph.name: clinical-sme
@graph.title: Clinical / scientific SME
@graph.description: Reviewer whose judgement is about the subject matter rather than the artefact.

@graph.name: administrator
@graph.title: Administrator
@graph.description: Administers the role graph itself: who exists, what they may act as, and what they may do. The ONE lane whose activities change the substrate every other diagram's lanes bind to — which is why it is drawn rather than left as a filesystem edit. Declared 2026-09-20 on the owner's answer that administration is a swimlane; `role-model.md`'s rule is that a role is never invented to make a diagram drawable, so it waited for that.

@graph.name: programme-manager
@graph.title: Programme manager
@graph.description: Owns what gets worked on and holds release authority. The lane that authorises, and the one step no policy may relax.

@graph.name: publication-manager
@graph.title: Publication manager
@graph.description: Takes an authorised release to its published form and is accountable for what is live.

@graph.name: business-analyst
@graph.title: Business analyst
@graph.description: Turns a stated need into a modelled requirement. Owns the CRDM lane and the BPMN/DMN that come out of it.

@graph.name: terminologist
@graph.title: Terminologist
@graph.description: Owns coded concepts and value sets — the vocabulary a DAK is expressed in.

@graph.name: fhir-modeller
@graph.title: FHIR modeller
@graph.description: Authors the L3 profiles, extensions and examples an IG is built from.

@graph.name: translation-coordinator
@graph.title: Translation coordinator
@graph.description: Decides what is translated, into which languages, and when a translation is accepted.

@graph.name: translator
@graph.title: Human translator
@graph.description: Produces the target-language text. Distinct from the coordinator because accepting one's own translation is the gate this separation removes.

@graph.name: translation-adjudicator
@graph.title: Translation adjudicator
@graph.description: Adjudicator who settles a disagreement between machine and human translation. The first specialisation of `adjudicator`, and the only one that existed before the role did — its lane documentation in translation-workflow.bpmn is where "a reviewer reports, an adjudicator settles" was written down.

@graph.name: adjudicator
@graph.title: Adjudicator
@graph.description: Settles a criterion whose reviewer entries disagree, and records WHY. Inherits `reviewer` because an adjudicator is a reviewer with one added entitlement — the `adjudication` permission — and the separation is the point: a reviewer reports, an adjudicator settles, and a process where every reviewer could settle has no way to say who decided. The KNOWLEDGE spreads (several roles carry the `adjudication` skill, because each has to tell an adjudicable disagreement from a complaint); the ENTITLEMENT does not, and lives on the actor as a permission.

@graph.name: feedback-provider
@graph.title: Feedback provider
@graph.description: Offers a finding on content or code — a script checker, a review agent, a reader, an SME. PLURAL by design: an adjudication is the judgement of one or more feedback providers' feedback, and the process draws the lane once for any number of them. Not an adjudicator: this role states what it found and on what evidence, and has no entitlement to settle the disagreement its finding creates.

@graph.name: stakeholder
@graph.title: Stakeholder
@graph.description: Signs off that a requirement is met. Carries no skills deliberately: sign-off is a judgement, not a procedure, and a skill here would suggest an agent could supply it.

@graph.name: authoring-agent
@graph.title: Authoring agent
@graph.description: The session agent doing the work. The broadest skill set here, and the one whose membership most needs auditing.

@graph.name: onboarding-agent
@graph.title: Onboarding agent
@graph.description: The authoring agent acting before there is a folio: clarifying what the user means by "create a folio", scanning an existing repo, and scaffolding.

@graph.name: ingestion-agent
@graph.title: Ingestion engine
@graph.description: Runs unattended over a source corpus. No user is in the room, so every gate it reaches must be decidable from the material.

@graph.name: librarian
@graph.title: Librarian
@graph.description: Acquires a source and files it. Distinct from `ingestion-agent`, which DERIVES structure from a source already in hand: this role decides what to capture, how faithfully, and what must be recorded at the moment of capture because nobody can reconstruct it later.

@graph.name: deep-researcher
@graph.title: Deep researcher
@graph.description: Answers a question FROM a corpus already held, and is answerable for the answer. Distinct from `librarian`, which decides what to capture, and from `ingestion-agent`, which derives structure from what was captured: both produce the corpus, and this role consumes it. Added 2026-09-23 with the `doc-researcher` methodology, because the accountability it names — somebody who must stand behind a synthesis and its citations — belonged to no declared role. THE LANE IT BINDS IS DRAWN IN ANOTHER INSTANCE — the `Deep researcher` lane of `folio-assistant-core/processes/deep-document-research.bpmn`, which names this role with `<folio:role ref>`. It carried a `lanes[]` here for about an hour on 2026-09-23 before #1168 landed and inverted the relation: a lane names its role, and a role does not list its lanes, because a general node never names its users. The binding is therefore stated once, on the lane, and this role says nothing about where it is drawn.

@graph.name: evidence-agent
@graph.title: Evidence agent
@graph.description: Retrieves and appraises external evidence for a guideline claim.

@graph.name: sibling-session
@graph.title: Sibling session
@graph.description: Another agent or human working the same store. Present in bean-lifecycle precisely to mark what is NOT yours to close.

@graph.name: build-pipeline
@graph.title: Build pipeline
@graph.description: Validates, renders and publishes, and watches whether that actually worked. A system lane: it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, so anything needing a decision belongs in a different lane. It carries `todo-manager` for the two CI-watcher dispatch points in `content-change-review`, which `claim` and `note` a bean and never `resolve` one -- claim is idempotent and note appends, both fixed programs, while deciding that a publish SUCCEEDED is the judgement this lane must not make (bean xom7: docs-site.yml failed 30 times while reporting its own exit code).

@graph.name: board-renderer
@graph.title: Board renderer
@graph.description: Draws a board and performs what the reader has already decided: reads each kind's declared zoom threshold and the layout layer, swaps a card for its avatar, projects an open window onto the canvas, and carries out a confirmed relocation. A system lane — it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, which is exactly why every decision in board-open-close.bpmn and board-relocate.bpmn sits in the reader's lane instead. It is NOT the build pipeline: it runs where the reader is, once per request, and publishes nothing.

@graph.name: validation-pipeline
@graph.title: Validation pipeline
@graph.description: The mechanical half of the HCI validation gate. Its findings are inputs to the editor's decision, never the decision.

@graph.name: publish-target
@graph.title: Publish target
@graph.description: GitHub Pages, or wherever the folio is served from. Reached, probed and reported on — never assumed live.

@graph.name: lean-toolchain
@graph.title: Lean toolchain
@graph.description: Elaborates and checks the formal half of a paper folio. Answers only what Lean can answer.

@graph.name: ig-publisher-service
@graph.title: IG publisher + validator
@graph.description: The JVM services an IG build shells out to. External in behaviour, internal in configuration.

@graph.name: attestation-service
@graph.title: Attestation service
@graph.description: Signs a QA report's run hashes over an API. A MECHANICAL role, and the one that DISAPPEARS when the actor performing it cannot reach out — which is why the signing process carries a second, human lane rather than a retry.

@graph.name: work-plan
@graph.title: Work plan (beans)
@graph.description: The shared store, modelled as a lane because tasks act ON it and a reader needs to see where the plan is touched. No actor takes this role on; it is acted upon.

@graph.name: corpus
@graph.title: Corpus
@graph.description: The versioned content store and the L1 source knowledge graph. Like the work plan, a lane that is written to rather than a participant that acts.

@graph.name: external-registry
@graph.title: External registry
@graph.description: Trusted registries and observatories outside this instance's control. Carries no skills because nothing here instructs it.

@graph.name: log
@graph.title: Activity log
@graph.description: The agent activity log. A MECHANICAL role and an `actedUpon` one: it is written to at task start and task end, and emptied by an actor — one entry, all of them, or on a periodic sweep — and it decides nothing. Modelled on `work-plan` and `corpus`, the two existing stores that are acted upon rather than acting. Its entries are held in the instance's unpublished store and never reach a published graph; the `activity-log` skill names the location, which is deliberately not repeated here because a role description IS published.

@graph.name: session-record
@graph.title: Session record
@graph.description: A session's context — who is acting, which instances are open, what it waits on. A MECHANICAL role and an `actedUpon` one: written to as the session moves and read by a sibling deciding whether a claim is live, and it decides nothing. Modelled on `work-plan`, `corpus` and `log`, the stores that are acted upon rather than acting. It carries `session-context` because the shape of what is written IS the discipline here — unlike `work-plan`, whose store has a CLI, this one is written by a machine that may be an LLM playing the part, so the schema is the contract.

@graph.name: editorial-authoring-agent
@graph.title: Editorial authoring agent
@graph.description: The authoring agent in the editorial lane: auditing a block's prose, structure and sourcing rather than writing new subject matter.

@graph.name: docs-authoring-agent
@graph.title: Docs authoring agent
@graph.description: The authoring agent producing what a person reads ABOUT the instance — generated references, the glossary, sticky notes, theme art and deployment documentation.

@graph.name: platform-authoring-agent
@graph.title: Platform authoring agent
@graph.description: The authoring agent working on how this instance PUBLISHES itself — the MCP projection, its contract, and the rendering endpoints.

@graph.name: session-coordinator
@graph.title: Session coordinator
@graph.description: The authoring agent managing the SESSION rather than the content: what this session intends, what is already in flight elsewhere, and what to pick up next.

@graph.name: integration-watcher
@graph.title: Integration watcher
@graph.description: Watches the default branch and open branches for newly-landed work that an existing audit axis should be re-run over. Reports findings; does not author the fix.

@graph.name: lean-authoring-agent
@graph.title: Lean authoring agent
@graph.description: Writes and repairs the Lean 4 formalization — translating narrative mathematics into declarations, keeping the build green, and curating what is staged for upstream.

@graph.name: proof-review-agent
@graph.title: Proof review agent
@graph.description: Reviews proofs — narrative and formal — for gaps, vacuity, redundancy and divergence between the two renderings of the same claim.

@graph.name: compute-authoring-agent
@graph.title: Compute authoring agent
@graph.description: Writes and audits the computation scripts and simulators that produce witnessed values, and keeps the paper's numbers and its computations from drifting apart.

@graph.name: tools
@graph.description: Tool definitions, one subdirectory per contributing instance (tools/<stub>/) so a composed instance adds its own without colliding on a filename. tools/index.ts merges them and is the only path a consumer imports. Authored as .ts calling defineTool so a malformed node fails at tsc; the JSON-LD and JSON Schema renderings are generated.

@graph.name: external-schemas
@graph.description: The specifications this instance depends on, one record per specification, each pinning the EDITION in use and carrying the operative terms DERIVED from the corpus rather than hand-listed. Owner, 2026-09-20: "dont need to materalize, but should reference specific version being used" and "some schema that is operational should be in KG". UNDECLARED UNTIL 2026-09-22, which is the dh4f shape inverted: dh4f is a declared directory nothing holds, reported as a clean scan; this was a held directory nothing declared, so every consumer that fans out over declared directories skipped a registry that pins four external namespaces. It was reachable only by the one script that hardcodes its path. `dependents: reproduce` because a dependent folio consumes its own specifications — it inherits the convention, an id and a relative path, not this instance's records.

@graph.name: code-lists
@graph.description: Closed sets of codes, one `"$schema": "folio-code-list/v1"` file per list, each code carrying a label, a definition, a source and, where it stands for one, a value. Owner, 2026-09-23: "we need an expandable option, not just declared in code. list of codes and corresponding narrative desc and source should be part of a node/asset", and SKOS as the published form. Two consumers today: adjudication steps name the list their `codes` come from (`<folio:adjudication list="…">`, checked when a diagram loads), and `schemas/namespaces.ts` reads every namespace this project mints from `own-namespaces.json` instead of carrying them as constants. Exported as SKOS concept schemes to `_kg/<stub>-code-lists.jsonld` by `scripts/glossary-export.ts`, beside the swimlane glossary. `dependents: skip` — a dependent INHERITS these through the dependency overlay (`codeListDirs`), and declares its own directory only when it has a list of its own.

@graph.name: schemas
@graph.description: The content-object model and the per-skill JSON Schemas. Declares BOTH graphs: the schema definitions themselves, and `kg` because a schema IS a knowledge-graph node — the .ts files are part of the KG, not a separate island beside it.

@graph.name: uml
@graph.description: UML class diagrams of every named sub-graph a harness declares — uml/overview/<instance>.puml|.mmd and uml/overview/<instance>/<sub-graph>.puml|.mmd — written from one model by scripts/gen-uml-overview.ts. The groupings are the declaration entries themselves and the classes are read from each graph kind's registered validator, so nothing here is authored. The rendered pages are docs/uml/overview/, which show the PlantUML rendering (docs/assets/img/uml/overview/, stamped with its source's hash) with the Mermaid beneath it, and link both sources. Owner, 2026-09-23.

@graph.name: skills
@graph.description: The knowledge graph. Skill packages, and the four other node kinds that point at them: `roles/roles.json` (a role IS a BPMN swimlane, and carries the skills its lane's activities need), `workflows/*.bpmn` + `workflows/decisions/*.dmn` (the processes those roles act in, reached through the skill that describes them), `requirements/*.json` (conformance obligations whose `satisfiedBy` names the skill or capability discharging them), `permissions/permissions.json` (what an actor may DO in any lane, as opposed to what its lane's role knows), Its audit verdicts are NOT here: they moved to the `qa` tree on 2026-09-19, because a verdict is a QA reviewer's output and placement follows provenance. Its id is `skills`, so its qualified name is `cat-harness.skills`; it was `cat-harness` until 2026-09-23 (bean iwtn), and `resolveDirectories` still reads that id as this one. Ids are stable across a relocation, paths are not. The `skills` graph does NOT owe a visualiser: `owesVisualiser` is `!renderable && holds !== "content"`, and `skills` is `content` — *"a graph that stands on its own does not need a viewer to be legible"*. So no gate was failing. What WAS wrong is that the viewer already existed and nothing declared it: `docs-auto` renders one sub-page per skills directory, and `graph-tiles.undeclaredProjections` lists exactly a directory with a published page and no declared visualisation — so all seven read as "no published viewer" in the navbar tiles while being rendered the whole time. `tools` is the same `content` kind and has declared one all along, which is the precedent: declaring a visualiser for a content kind is a courtesy the corpus already extends, not an obligation this invents.

@graph.name: scenarios
@graph.description: Scenarios — the Roles an Actor takes on, in `roles.json`, and the User Stories told as them, in `stories.json`. A Role IS a BPMN swimlane: it carries the Skills its lane's activities need and the Actor kinds that may play it; a lane names its Role, and a story names the Role it is told as, so the Role lists neither (#1168). SPLIT OUT OF `skills/` on 2026-09-21 so that "give me the Scenarios" is a query on the kind rather than a match on a path.

@graph.name: policies
@graph.description: What an Actor may DO, as W3C ODRL 2.2 policies (issue #1180, owner 2026-09-23). `folio-defaults.jsonld` is the instance's odrl:Set: the permissions each actor file used to list, migrated one rule per (actor, action), plus the owner's floor for an unauthenticated reader (visualize and render only). Actions are the folio ODRL profile in `skills/permissions/permissions.json`; roles stay in `scenarios/`, and identity (which login is which actor) stays in the data store, never here. `dependents: skip` because a downstream instance writes its own policies and inherits these through ODRL's `inheritFrom`, rather than getting a copy.

@graph.name: processes
@graph.description: Executable BPMN processes and the DMN tables their gateways compute from. The diagrams are the source of truth, not illustrations of one: a lane binds a Role, an activity names the Skill to run through `<folio:skill ref>`, and `workflow_complete` refuses a step that is not enabled. WHERE A RUNNING INSTANCE GOT TO is not here — that is `beans/workflows/`, kind `workflow-state`, which is `state` rather than `content`. Two questions, two graphs.

It points at the `docs-auto` index, NOT at the mount route `/docs/<instance>/`: that mount is a VERBATIM copy of the directory, and `visualiserHref` exists precisely because linking a rail to it lands on a byte-identical page — the owner's *"clicking on doc/ ... under who-iris navbar did nothing"*.
